---- MODULE W4Od17m1p6t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Sorters, MaxRound

Grants == [to : Sorters, rnd : 1..MaxRound]

VARIABLES sorter, wire, taken, issued

vars == <<sorter, wire, taken, issued>>

Typing ==
    /\ sorter \in [Sorters -> [state : {"idle", "working"}, rnd : 0..MaxRound]]
    /\ wire \subseteq Grants
    /\ taken \subseteq Grants
    /\ issued \in 0..MaxRound

Init ==
    /\ sorter = [n \in Sorters |-> [state |-> "idle", rnd |-> 0]]
    /\ wire = {}
    /\ taken = {}
    /\ issued = 0

\* The right to commit routing decisions moves round the ring as a numbered
\* grant.  Grants sit on an unordered wire, so a sorter can be handed an old
\* grant after a newer one has already reached it.
PassOn(n) ==
    /\ issued < MaxRound
    /\ issued' = issued + 1
    /\ wire' = wire \cup {[to |-> n, rnd |-> issued + 1]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<sorter, taken>>

\* A sorter takes a grant only if its round is newer than the round the sorter
\* has already moved to, and it records the grant it acted on.
Take(g) ==
    /\ g \in wire
    /\ sorter[g.to].state = "idle"
    /\ g.rnd > sorter[g.to].rnd
    /\ sorter' = [sorter EXCEPT ![g.to] = [state |-> "working", rnd |-> g.rnd]]
    /\ taken' = taken \cup {g}
    /\ wire' = wire \ {g}
    /\ UNCHANGED issued

\* A grant that arrives behind one the sorter has already moved past is stale
\* and is dropped rather than acted on; so is one that finds the sorter busy.
Drop(g) ==
    /\ g \in wire
    /\ \/ g.rnd <= sorter[g.to].rnd
       \/ sorter[g.to].state = "working"
    /\ wire' = wire \ {g}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<sorter, taken, issued>>

\* Committing the routing decisions of a round hands the ring back.
Release(n) ==
    /\ sorter[n].state = "working"
    /\ sorter' = [sorter EXCEPT ![n].state = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<wire, taken, issued>>

Quiet ==
    /\ issued = MaxRound
    /\ wire = {}
    /\ \A n \in Sorters : sorter[n].state = "idle"
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Sorters : PassOn(n) \/ Release(n)
    \/ \E g \in Grants : Take(g) \/ Drop(g)
    \/ Quiet

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(\E n \in Sorters : Release(n))
    /\ WF_vars(\E g \in Grants : Drop(g))

\* A sorter that is committing routing decisions is doing so under a grant it
\* actually took, at exactly the round it took: nothing is ever committed on
\* the strength of a grant the ring has moved past.
NoStaleAuthority ==
    \A n \in Sorters :
        (sorter[n].state = "working") =>
            (Cardinality({g \in taken : g.to = n /\ g.rnd = sorter[n].rnd}) = 1)

EveryHolderEventuallyHandsBack ==
    \A n \in Sorters : (sorter[n].state = "working") ~> (sorter[n].state = "idle")

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Sorters = {srtPierA, srtPierB, srtPierC}
    MaxRound = 3

INVARIANT NoStaleAuthority
PROPERTY EveryHolderEventuallyHandsBack
nl:
An airport baggage router splits its sorting across a ring of sorter nodes. The right to commit routing decisions moves round that ring as a numbered grant: at any moment only the node currently holding a grant may commit decisions, because two nodes committing at once would send the same bag down two chutes.

Grants travel over the baggage network, which gives no ordering guarantee whatsoever. A grant sits on an unordered wire, and a sorter can be handed an old grant after a newer one has already reached it. A sorter therefore takes a grant only if its round number is newer than the round the sorter has already moved to, and it records which grant it acted on.

A grant that arrives behind one the sorter has already moved past is stale: the sorter drops it rather than acting on it, because acting on it would mean committing decisions on authority the ring has already taken away. A grant that finds a sorter already busy is dropped for the same reason.

When a sorter has committed the routing decisions for its round it hands the ring back and goes idle. Once the last round has been issued, the wire is clear and every sorter is idle, the ring is quiet.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A sorter that is committing routing decisions is doing so under a grant it actually took, at exactly the round it took it, so nothing is ever committed on the strength of a grant the ring has already moved past.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: A sorter that has taken the ring always eventually hands it back.

---- MODULE W4Od1m6p1t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Amends, Sectors, Desks, Horizon, LeaseTicks, NoDesk

ASSUME NoDesk \notin Desks

Clip(n) == IF n < Horizon THEN n ELSE Horizon

VARIABLES amend, plan, lease, clock

vars == <<amend, plan, lease, clock>>

Typing ==
    /\ amend \in [Amends -> [state : {"raised", "inflight", "booked"},
                             sect : Sectors \cup {NoDesk}]]
    /\ plan \in [Sectors -> SUBSET Amends]
    /\ lease \in [Sectors -> [holder : Desks \cup {NoDesk}, until : 0..Horizon]]
    /\ clock \in 0..Horizon

Init ==
    /\ amend = [a \in Amends |-> [state |-> "raised", sect |-> NoDesk]]
    /\ plan = [s \in Sectors |-> {}]
    /\ lease = [s \in Sectors |-> [holder |-> NoDesk, until |-> 0]]
    /\ clock = 0

\* A control desk takes a lease on a sector's flight plan.  Leases run out on
\* the clock so a desk that goes quiet cannot hold a sector for ever.
TakeLease(d, s) ==
    /\ lease[s].holder = NoDesk
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![s] = [holder |-> d, until |-> Clip(clock + LeaseTicks)]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<amend, plan, clock>>

\* An amendment is put on the sector datalink.  The link reorders freely, so
\* amendments raised in one order can reach the plan in any other.
Send(a, s) ==
    /\ amend[a].state = "raised"
    /\ lease[s].holder # NoDesk
    /\ amend' = [amend EXCEPT ![a] = [state |-> "inflight", sect |-> s]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<plan, lease, clock>>

\* An amendment is written into the sector plan only while the desk that sent
\* it still holds a live lease on that sector, and writing it adds to the plan
\* rather than replacing it, so nothing already booked is displaced.
Book(a) ==
    /\ amend[a].state = "inflight"
    /\ lease[amend[a].sect].holder # NoDesk
    /\ lease[amend[a].sect].until > clock
    /\ plan' = [plan EXCEPT ![amend[a].sect] = plan[amend[a].sect] \cup {a}]
    /\ amend' = [amend EXCEPT ![a].state = "booked"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, clock>>

Tick ==
    /\ clock < Horizon
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<amend, plan, lease>>

Expire(s) ==
    /\ lease[s].holder # NoDesk
    /\ lease[s].until <= clock
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![s] = [holder |-> NoDesk, until |-> 0]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<amend, plan, clock>>

\* A sector plan is tidied of amendments that never got booked; a booked
\* amendment is left exactly where it is.
Tidy(s) ==
    /\ plan' = [plan EXCEPT ![s] = {a \in plan[s] : amend[a].state = "booked"}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<amend, lease, clock>>

Quiet ==
    /\ \A a \in Amends : amend[a].state = "booked"
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Desks, s \in Sectors : TakeLease(d, s)
    \/ \E a \in Amends, s \in Sectors : Send(a, s)
    \/ \E a \in Amends : Book(a)
    \/ \E s \in Sectors : Expire(s) \/ Tidy(s)
    \/ Tick
    \/ Quiet

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every amendment that has been booked stands in exactly one sector plan, so
\* a booked flight-plan change is never carried away by a later write, a lease
\* running out, or a tidy-up.
NoLostAmendment ==
    \A a \in Amends :
        (amend[a].state = "booked") =>
            (Cardinality({s \in Sectors : a \in plan[s]}) = 1)

====
nl:
An air-traffic centre holds a flight plan per sector, and control desks amend those plans as traffic develops. A desk may only write into a sector's plan while it holds a lease on that sector, and leases run out on the clock rather than being held until the desk gives them up, so a desk that goes quiet cannot hold a sector for the rest of the watch.

Amendments travel over the sector datalink, which reorders freely: amendments raised in one order can reach the plans in any other, and there is no way for a desk to know which of its amendments has landed first. An amendment is put on the link against a sector that some desk currently holds.

An amendment is written into the sector plan only while there is still a live lease on that sector -- one that the clock has not yet run past. Writing adds the amendment to the plan rather than replacing the plan wholesale, so nothing already booked there is displaced by a write that was prepared against an older view. A lease the clock has run past is released and the sector goes back to being unheld.

Sector plans are tidied from time to time of amendments that were put on the link but never got booked; an amendment that has been booked is left exactly where it is. Once every amendment is booked the watch is quiet.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every amendment that has been booked stands in exactly one sector plan, so a booked flight-plan change is never carried away by a later write, by a lease running out, or by a tidy-up.

---- MODULE W4Od13m3p6t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Machines, Desks, MaxEpoch, NoDesk

ASSUME NoDesk \notin Desks

Epochs == 1..MaxEpoch
Loads == [mach : Machines, ep : Epochs]

VARIABLES machine, claim, boss, loaded, bricked

vars == <<machine, claim, boss, loaded, bricked>>

Typing ==
    /\ machine \in [Machines -> [state : {"stale", "current"}, ep : 0..MaxEpoch]]
    /\ claim \in [Desks -> 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ boss \in [desk : Desks \cup {NoDesk}, ep : 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ loaded \subseteq Loads
    /\ bricked \subseteq Machines

Init ==
    /\ machine = [m \in Machines |-> [state |-> "current", ep |-> 0]]
    /\ claim = [d \in Desks |-> 0]
    /\ boss = [desk |-> NoDesk, ep |-> 0]
    /\ loaded = {}
    /\ bricked = {}

\* Price authority moves between the regional desks by epoch.  A desk claims an
\* epoch newer than any yet claimed by anybody.
Claim(d, e) ==
    /\ \A k \in Desks : e > claim[k]
    /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![d] = e]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<machine, boss, loaded, bricked>>

\* Taking authority makes every machine still carrying an older price schedule
\* stale, so a machine cannot go on selling at a schedule the network has left.
TakeOver(d) ==
    /\ claim[d] > boss.ep
    /\ boss' = [desk |-> d, ep |-> claim[d]]
    /\ machine' = [m \in Machines |->
                     IF machine[m].ep < claim[d]
                     THEN [state |-> "stale", ep |-> machine[m].ep]
                     ELSE machine[m]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<claim, loaded, bricked>>

\* Only the desk that currently holds authority may push a schedule, and the
\* machine records the epoch it was loaded under.  A push from a desk that has
\* been superseded carries an older epoch and simply cannot land.
Push(m) ==
    /\ boss.desk # NoDesk
    /\ m \notin bricked
    /\ machine[m].ep < boss.ep
    /\ machine' = [machine EXCEPT ![m] = [state |-> "current", ep |-> boss.ep]]
    /\ loaded' = loaded \cup {[mach |-> m, ep |-> boss.ep]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<claim, boss, bricked>>

\* A single machine may lose its modem and go off the network without saying
\* so; it then carries whatever schedule it last had.
Brick(m) ==
    /\ bricked = {}
    /\ bricked' = {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<machine, claim, boss, loaded>>

Quiet ==
    /\ \A m \in Machines : machine[m].state = "current" \/ m \in bricked
    /\ \A d \in Desks : claim[d] = MaxEpoch \/ boss.ep = MaxEpoch
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Desks, e \in Epochs : Claim(d, e)
    \/ \E d \in Desks : TakeOver(d)
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Push(m) \/ Brick(m)
    \/ Quiet

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(\E d \in Desks, e \in Epochs : Claim(d, e))
    /\ WF_vars(\E d \in Desks : TakeOver(d))
    /\ WF_vars(\E m \in Machines : Push(m))

\* A machine that is selling at the current schedule was loaded with exactly
\* that schedule under exactly the epoch it is carrying, so no machine is ever
\* selling on the authority of a desk the network has superseded.
NoStaleSchedule ==
    \A m \in Machines :
        (machine[m].state = "current" /\ machine[m].ep > 0) =>
            (Cardinality({x \in loaded : x.mach = m /\ x.ep = machine[m].ep}) = 1)

EveryMachineEventuallyCatchesUp ==
    \A m \in Machines :
        (machine[m].state = "stale") ~>
            (machine[m].state = "current" \/ m \in bricked)

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Machines = {vmConcourse, vmDepot}
    Desks = {dskEast, dskWest}
    MaxEpoch = 2
    NoDesk = nilDesk

INVARIANT NoStaleSchedule
PROPERTY EveryMachineEventuallyCatchesUp
nl:
A vending machine network sells at prices pushed out from a regional desk. Only one desk holds pricing authority at a time, and authority moves between the desks by epoch: a desk takes it by claiming an epoch number strictly newer than any epoch yet claimed by anybody.

Taking authority makes every machine that is still carrying an older schedule stale, because a machine selling at a schedule the network has moved on from is exactly the case the operator has to avoid -- a superseded desk's prices in the field are unauthorised prices.

Only the desk that currently holds authority may push a schedule out, and a machine records the epoch it was loaded under when it takes one. A push from a desk that has been superseded carries an older epoch than the machine is already at and simply cannot land, so a stale desk cannot reprice the estate behind the current desk's back.

Machines in the field are not reliable. A single machine may lose its modem and drop off the network without saying so, after which it goes on carrying whatever schedule it last took and no push can reach it; the rest of the estate carries on being repriced normally.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A machine that is selling at the current schedule was loaded with exactly that schedule under exactly the epoch it is carrying, so no machine is ever selling on the authority of a desk the network has superseded.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every machine left stale by a change of pricing authority eventually catches up to the current schedule, unless it has dropped off the network altogether.

---- MODULE W4Od16m7p5t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Batches, Benches, MinWitness, MaxRev

Entries == [btc : Batches, rev : 1..MaxRev]

VARIABLES batch, book, rev, manned

vars == <<batch, book, rev, manned>>

Typing ==
    /\ batch \in [Batches -> [state : {"stored", "drawn", "destroyed", "returned"},
                              base : 0..MaxRev]]
    /\ book \subseteq Entries
    /\ rev \in 0..MaxRev
    /\ manned \subseteq Benches

Init ==
    /\ batch = [b \in Batches |-> [state |-> "stored", base |-> 0]]
    /\ book = {}
    /\ rev = 0
    /\ manned = Benches

\* Witness benches are manned and stood down through the shift, so the number
\* of witnesses available to a destruction changes while the round is running.
StandDown(w) ==
    /\ w \in manned
    /\ manned' = manned \ {w}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<batch, book, rev>>

ManUp(w) ==
    /\ w \notin manned
    /\ manned' = manned \cup {w}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<batch, book, rev>>

\* A batch is drawn from the safe against the revision the destruction book
\* currently carries.
Draw(b) ==
    /\ batch[b].state = "stored"
    /\ rev < MaxRev
    /\ batch' = [batch EXCEPT ![b] = [state |-> "drawn", base |-> rev]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, rev, manned>>

\* Destruction is irreversible: the batch is denatured and gone, and the book
\* entry can never be unwritten.  The write into the book is a compare-and-swap
\* against the revision the batch was drawn on, so a batch drawn twice cannot
\* be written twice; enough benches must also be manned to witness it.
Destroy(b) ==
    /\ batch[b].state = "drawn"
    /\ batch[b].base = rev
    /\ Cardinality(manned) >= MinWitness
    /\ rev < MaxRev
    /\ book' = book \cup {[btc |-> b, rev |-> rev + 1]}
    /\ rev' = rev + 1
    /\ batch' = [batch EXCEPT ![b].state = "destroyed"]
    /\ UNCHANGED manned

\* A batch that cannot be destroyed on this pass -- the book has moved on, or
\* there are not enough witnesses -- goes back into the safe intact.
Return(b) ==
    /\ batch[b].state = "drawn"
    /\ \/ batch[b].base # rev
       \/ Cardinality(manned) < MinWitness
    /\ batch' = [batch EXCEPT ![b].state = "returned"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, rev, manned>>

Restock(b) ==
    /\ batch[b].state = "returned"
    /\ batch' = [batch EXCEPT ![b].state = "stored"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, rev, manned>>

Shut ==
    /\ rev = MaxRev
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E w \in Benches : StandDown(w) \/ ManUp(w)
    \/ \E b \in Batches : Draw(b) \/ Destroy(b) \/ Return(b) \/ Restock(b)
    \/ Shut

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A batch that has been destroyed stands exactly once in the destruction book,
\* however many times it was drawn from the safe and put back.
DestroyedOnce ==
    \A b \in Batches :
        (batch[b].state = "destroyed") =>
            (Cardinality({x \in book : x.btc = b}) = 1)

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Batches = {btcMorphA, btcMorphB}
    Benches = {bnPrep, bnCheck, bnSign}
    MinWitness = 2
    MaxRev = 3

INVARIANT DestroyedOnce
nl:
A hospital pharmacy destroys expired controlled drugs against a destruction book. The book is the legal record of what was denatured and when, and it is written through a single register carrying a revision number.

Witness benches are manned and stood down through the shift as staff move between duties, so the number of witnesses available to a destruction changes while the round is running. A destruction needs at least a set number of benches manned at the moment it happens.

A batch is drawn from the safe against the revision the destruction book currently carries. Destroying it is irreversible: the batch is denatured and gone, and the book entry can never be unwritten or amended. The write into the book is a compare-and-swap against the revision the batch was drawn on, and landing bumps that revision -- so a batch that was drawn twice, because it was put back and drawn again, cannot be written into the book twice.

A batch that cannot be destroyed on this pass -- because the book has moved on since it was drawn, or because there are not enough benches manned to witness it -- goes back into the safe intact and can be restocked and drawn again later. Once the register has been stamped for the last time in the round the safe is shut.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A batch that has been destroyed stands exactly once in the destruction book, however many times it was drawn from the safe and put back.

---- MODULE W4Od17m4p5t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Bags, Chutes, QueueCap, MaxScan

VARIABLES bag, queue, manifest, jammed

vars == <<bag, queue, manifest, jammed>>

Typing ==
    /\ bag \in [Bags -> [state : {"arriving", "queued", "scanning", "dropped"},
                         scans : 0..MaxScan]]
    /\ queue \subseteq Bags
    /\ manifest \subseteq [bag : Bags, chute : Chutes]
    /\ jammed \subseteq Chutes

Init ==
    /\ bag = [b \in Bags |-> [state |-> "arriving", scans |-> 0]]
    /\ queue = {}
    /\ manifest = {}
    /\ jammed = {}

\* The sorter's read queue is short.  While it is full a bag stays on the belt
\* and goes round again rather than being taken, which is the backpressure the
\* pier relies on to keep the sorter from being swamped.
Admit(b) ==
    /\ bag[b].state = "arriving"
    /\ Cardinality(queue) < QueueCap
    /\ queue' = queue \cup {b}
    /\ bag' = [bag EXCEPT ![b].state = "queued"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<manifest, jammed>>

Pick(b) ==
    /\ bag[b].state = "queued"
    /\ bag' = [bag EXCEPT ![b].state = "scanning"]
    /\ queue' = queue \ {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<manifest, jammed>>

\* Reading a bag tag takes several looks.  Readers here are slow but never
\* fail: a bag may sit under the head for a long time before its tag resolves.
Look(b) ==
    /\ bag[b].state = "scanning"
    /\ bag[b].scans < MaxScan
    /\ bag' = [bag EXCEPT ![b].scans = bag[b].scans + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, manifest, jammed>>

\* Dropping a bag into a chute is irreversible: it is over the lip and into the
\* cart, and it can never be dropped a second time.  The drop is recorded on
\* the flight manifest as it happens.
Drop(b, k) ==
    /\ bag[b].state = "scanning"
    /\ bag[b].scans = MaxScan
    /\ k \notin jammed
    /\ manifest' = manifest \cup {[bag |-> b, chute |-> k]}
    /\ bag' = [bag EXCEPT ![b].state = "dropped"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, jammed>>

\* A chute can jam, but the pier is never worked with every chute jammed.
Jam(k) ==
    /\ k \notin jammed
    /\ Cardinality(jammed) + 1 < Cardinality(Chutes)
    /\ jammed' = jammed \cup {k}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bag, queue, manifest>>

Clear(k) ==
    /\ k \in jammed
    /\ jammed' = jammed \ {k}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bag, queue, manifest>>

Quiet ==
    /\ \A b \in Bags : bag[b].state = "dropped"
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Bags : Admit(b) \/ Pick(b) \/ Look(b)
    \/ \E b \in Bags, k \in Chutes : Drop(b, k)
    \/ \E k \in Chutes : Jam(k) \/ Clear(k)
    \/ Quiet

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(\E b \in Bags : Pick(b))
    /\ WF_vars(\E b \in Bags : Look(b))
    /\ WF_vars(\E b \in Bags, k \in Chutes : Drop(b, k))

\* A bag that has gone over a chute lip appears exactly once on the flight
\* manifest, however long its tag took to read.
DroppedOnce ==
    \A b \in Bags :
        (bag[b].state = "dropped") =>
            (Cardinality({x \in manifest : x.bag = b}) = 1)

EveryQueuedBagEventuallyDrops ==
    \A b \in Bags : (bag[b].state = "queued") ~> (bag[b].state = "dropped")

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Bags = {bagRed, bagBlue}
    Chutes = {chtA, chtB}
    QueueCap = 1
    MaxScan = 2

INVARIANT DroppedOnce
PROPERTY EveryQueuedBagEventuallyDrops
nl:
An airport baggage router reads bags off a belt and drops them into chutes for their flights. The sorter's read queue is deliberately short: while it is full a bag simply stays on the belt and goes round again rather than being taken, which is the backpressure the pier relies on to keep the sorter from being swamped at a bank.

A bag taken off the belt goes under the read head. Reading a tag takes several looks -- the labels are creased, wet, or facing the wrong way -- and the readers here are slow but never fail: a bag may sit under the head for a long time before its tag finally resolves, but it always resolves in the end.

Dropping a bag into a chute is the irreversible step. Once the bag is over the lip it is in the cart and on its way to the aircraft; it cannot be pulled back, and it can never be dropped a second time. The drop is written onto the flight manifest as it happens, and that manifest is what the ramp loads against.

Chutes jam from time to time and a jammed chute takes nothing, but the pier is never worked with every chute jammed at once, and a jam is cleared and the chute goes back into use. Once every bag has been dropped the pier is quiet.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A bag that has gone over a chute lip appears exactly once on the flight manifest, however long its tag took to read.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every bag taken into the sorter's read queue is eventually dropped into a chute.

---- MODULE W4Od1m9p1t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Notes, Bands, MaxEpoch, NoBand

ASSUME NoBand \notin Bands

VARIABLES slip, owner, working, epoch

vars == <<slip, owner, working, epoch>>

Typing ==
    /\ slip \in [Notes -> [state : {"raised", "filed", "committed"},
                           ep : 0..MaxEpoch]]
    /\ owner \in [Notes -> Bands \cup {NoBand}]
    /\ working \subseteq Bands
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch

Init ==
    /\ slip = [n \in Notes |-> [state |-> "raised", ep |-> 0]]
    /\ owner = [n \in Notes |-> NoBand]
    /\ working = Bands
    /\ epoch = 0

\* A coordination slip is filed against a band that somebody is working, and
\* records the epoch the centre was configured under when it was filed.
File(n, b) ==
    /\ slip[n].state = "raised"
    /\ b \in working
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![n] = b]
    /\ slip' = [slip EXCEPT ![n] = [state |-> "filed", ep |-> epoch]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<working, epoch>>

\* Committing a slip is what the receiving controller is told about; once told
\* they work the traffic on it and never ask for it again.
Commit(n) ==
    /\ slip[n].state = "filed"
    /\ owner[n] \in working
    /\ slip' = [slip EXCEPT ![n].state = "committed"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, working, epoch>>

\* Re-sectorising under a strictly newer epoch.  Handing a band over carries
\* every slip filed against it to a band that stays worked, in the same
\* movement as the handover, so nothing is stranded in a band nobody has.
HandOver(b, c) ==
    /\ b \in working
    /\ c \in working
    /\ b # c
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ working' = working \ {b}
    /\ owner' = [n \in Notes |-> IF owner[n] = b THEN c ELSE owner[n]]
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED slip

\* Splitting a band back out puts it back on a controller's desk.
SplitOut(b) ==
    /\ b \notin working
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ working' = working \cup {b}
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<slip, owner>>

Quiet ==
    /\ \A n \in Notes : slip[n].state = "committed"
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Notes, b \in Bands : File(n, b)
    \/ \E n \in Notes : Commit(n)
    \/ \E b, c \in Bands : HandOver(b, c)
    \/ \E b \in Bands : SplitOut(b)
    \/ Quiet

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(\E n \in Notes, b \in Bands : File(n, b))
    /\ WF_vars(\E n \in Notes : Commit(n))

\* Every committed coordination slip still belongs to a band a controller is
\* actually working, so no committed slip is stranded by a re-sectorisation.
NoStrandedSlip ==
    \A n \in Notes :
        (slip[n].state = "committed") =>
            (Cardinality({b \in Bands : owner[n] = b /\ b \in working}) = 1)

EverySlipEventuallyCommitted ==
    \A n \in Notes : (slip[n].state = "raised") ~> (slip[n].state = "committed")

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Notes = {ntClimb, ntHandoff}
    Bands = {bndUpper, bndLower}
    MaxEpoch = 2
    NoBand = nilBand

INVARIANT NoStrandedSlip
PROPERTY EverySlipEventuallyCommitted
nl:
An air-traffic centre records coordination slips -- a climb clearance to be honoured, an agreement with the next centre -- against whichever band of airspace the traffic is in. A slip that has been committed is one the receiving controller has been told about: they work the traffic on it and never ask for it again, so a committed slip that ended up belonging to a band nobody is working would be an update lost in the worst possible place.

The centre re-sectorises during the watch, and each change carries a strictly newer epoch number. Bands are handed over between desks and split back out as traffic builds and thins, so the number of bands actually being worked changes while aircraft are in the air.

A slip is filed against a band somebody is currently working, and records the epoch the centre was configured under at the time. It is committed once it belongs to a band that is still being worked. Handing a band over carries every slip filed against it across to a band that stays worked, in the same movement as the handover itself, so nothing is stranded. Splitting a band back out puts it on a controller's desk again for new filings.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every committed coordination slip still belongs to a band that a controller is actually working, so no committed slip is stranded by a re-sectorisation.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every coordination slip that is raised is eventually committed.

---- MODULE W4Od3m0p0t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Desks, Rails, MaxRev, Legs, MaxCleared, NoDesk, NoRail

ASSUME NoDesk \notin Desks /\ NoRail \notin Rails

VARIABLES desk, rail, posted, cleared

vars == <<desk, rail, posted, cleared>>

Typing ==
    /\ desk \in [Desks -> [state : {"idle", "reading", "posting"},
                           base : 0..MaxRev, want : Rails \cup {NoRail}]]
    /\ rail \in [Rails -> [holder : Desks \cup {NoDesk}, rev : 0..MaxRev]]
    /\ posted \in [Desks -> 0..Legs]
    /\ cleared \in [Rails -> 0..MaxCleared]

Init ==
    /\ desk = [d \in Desks |-> [state |-> "idle", base |-> 0, want |-> NoRail]]
    /\ rail = [r \in Rails |-> [holder |-> NoDesk, rev |-> 0]]
    /\ posted = [d \in Desks |-> 0]
    /\ cleared = [r \in Rails |-> 0]

\* Two settlement instances run side by side over one pool of posting rails.
\* A desk reads the rail it wants and the revision stamped on it, then goes
\* away to assemble its batch.
Read(d, r) ==
    /\ desk[d].state = "idle"
    /\ desk' = [desk EXCEPT ![d] = [state |-> "reading", base |-> rail[r].rev,
                                    want |-> r]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rail, posted, cleared>>

\* Taking the rail is a compare-and-swap: it only lands while the revision the
\* desk read is still on the rail and nobody is standing on it.  That is what
\* stops the other instance walking onto the same rail behind this one's read.
Take(d) ==
    /\ desk[d].state = "reading"
    /\ rail[desk[d].want].rev = desk[d].base
    /\ rail[desk[d].want].holder = NoDesk
    /\ rail[desk[d].want].rev < MaxRev
    /\ rail' = [rail EXCEPT ![desk[d].want] = [holder |-> d,
                                               rev |-> rail[desk[d].want].rev + 1]]
    /\ desk' = [desk EXCEPT ![d].state = "posting"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<posted, cleared>>

\* A desk whose read has gone stale drops its batch and starts again.
Retry(d) ==
    /\ desk[d].state = "reading"
    /\ \/ rail[desk[d].want].rev # desk[d].base
       \/ rail[desk[d].want].holder # NoDesk
       \/ rail[desk[d].want].rev = MaxRev
    /\ desk' = [desk EXCEPT ![d] = [state |-> "idle", base |-> 0, want |-> NoRail]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rail, posted, cleared>>

PostLeg(d) ==
    /\ desk[d].state = "posting"
    /\ posted[d] < Legs
    /\ posted' = [posted EXCEPT ![d] = posted[d] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<desk, rail, cleared>>

StepOff(d) ==
    /\ desk[d].state = "posting"
    /\ posted[d] = Legs
    /\ rail' = [rail EXCEPT ![desk[d].want].holder = NoDesk]
    /\ desk' = [desk EXCEPT ![d] = [state |-> "idle", base |-> 0, want |-> NoRail]]
    /\ posted' = [posted EXCEPT ![d] = 0]
    /\ cleared' = [cleared EXCEPT ![desk[d].want] =
                      IF cleared[desk[d].want] < MaxCleared
                      THEN cleared[desk[d].want] + 1 ELSE MaxCleared]

Closed ==
    /\ \A r \in Rails : rail[r].rev = MaxRev
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Desks, r \in Rails : Read(d, r)
    \/ \E d \in Desks : Take(d) \/ Retry(d) \/ PostLeg(d) \/ StepOff(d)
    \/ Closed

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A desk that is posting is standing on exactly one rail, so the two
\* settlement instances never work the same rail at the same time.
RailExclusion ==
    \A d \in Desks :
        (desk[d].state = "posting") =>
            (Cardinality({r \in Rails : rail[r].holder = d}) = 1)

====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Desks = {dskDay, dskNight}
    Rails = {rlSterling, rlEuro}
    MaxRev = 2
    Legs = 2
    MaxCleared = 2
    NoDesk = nilDesk
    NoRail = nilRail

INVARIANT RailExclusion
nl:
A bank settles its interbank batches over a small pool of posting rails, one rail per currency. A rail is a critical resource: while one desk is standing on it walking a batch through, no other desk may touch it, because the rail rewrites the same reserve balances leg by leg and two batches interleaved would post against balances the other has already moved.

Two settlement instances run side by side over that one pool -- a day instance and a night instance, each with its own operators and its own batches -- so both are constantly reaching for the same rails. The rails are not held under a lock; each carries a revision stamp instead.

A desk reads the rail it wants together with the revision stamped on it, then goes away to assemble its batch. Taking the rail is a compare-and-swap: it lands only while the revision the desk read is still the one on the rail and nobody is standing on it, and taking it bumps that revision. That is exactly what stops the other instance walking onto the same rail behind this desk's read. A desk whose read has gone stale -- the revision has moved, or somebody is on the rail, or the rail has been stamped for the last time in the window -- drops its batch and starts again from a fresh read.

A desk standing on a rail posts its batch one leg at a time and steps off only when the whole batch is through, leaving the rail free for the next desk and adding one to that rail's tally of batches cleared in the window.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A desk that is posting is standing on exactly one rail, so the two settlement instances never work the same rail at the same time.

---- MODULE W4Od19m7p5t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Titles, Branches, MaxRev, Copies, NoBranch

ASSUME NoBranch \notin Branches

VARIABLES title, branch, register, stock

vars == <<title, branch, register, stock>>

Typing ==
    /\ title \in [Titles -> [state : {"held", "marked", "withdrawn"},
                             base : 0..MaxRev, by : Branches \cup {NoBranch}]]
    /\ branch \in [Branches -> [state : {"up", "dark"}, rev : 0..MaxRev]]
    /\ register \subseteq [ttl : Titles, br : Branches]
    /\ stock \in [Titles -> 0..Copies]

Init ==
    /\ title = [t \in Titles |-> [state |-> "held", base |-> 0, by |-> NoBranch]]
    /\ branch = [b \in Branches |-> [state |-> "up", rev |-> 0]]
    /\ register = {}
    /\ stock = [t \in Titles |-> Copies]

\* A branch marks a title for deaccession against the revision its own
\* catalogue register currently carries.
Mark(t, b) ==
    /\ title[t].state = "held"
    /\ branch[b].state = "up"
    /\ branch[b].rev < MaxRev
    /\ title' = [title EXCEPT ![t] = [state |-> "marked", base |-> branch[b].rev,
                                      by |-> b]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<branch, register, stock>>

\* Withdrawing a title is irreversible: the copies are pulped and the shelf
\* mark is retired, so it can never be withdrawn again.  The write into the
\* deaccession register is a compare-and-swap against the revision the mark was
\* taken on, which is what stops a title marked twice being pulped twice.
Withdraw(t) ==
    /\ title[t].state = "marked"
    /\ branch[title[t].by].state = "up"
    /\ branch[title[t].by].rev = title[t].base
    /\ register' = register \cup {[ttl |-> t, br |-> title[t].by]}
    /\ branch' = [branch EXCEPT ![title[t].by].rev = title[t].base + 1]
    /\ title' = [title EXCEPT ![t].state = "withdrawn"]
    /\ stock' = [stock EXCEPT ![t] = 0]

\* A mark that has gone stale, or whose branch has gone dark, is dropped and
\* the title stays on the shelf.
Unmark(t) ==
    /\ title[t].state = "marked"
    /\ \/ branch[title[t].by].state = "dark"
       \/ branch[title[t].by].rev # title[t].base
    /\ title' = [title EXCEPT ![t] = [state |-> "held", base |-> 0, by |-> NoBranch]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<branch, register, stock>>

\* One branch's catalogue node may drop off the consortium without saying so.
GoDark(b) ==
    /\ \A c \in Branches : branch[c].state = "up"
    /\ Cardinality(Branches) > 1
    /\ branch' = [branch EXCEPT ![b].state = "dark"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<title, register, stock>>

Quiet ==
    /\ \A t \in Titles : title[t].state = "withdrawn"
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Titles, b \in Branches : Mark(t, b)
    \/ \E t \in Titles : Withdraw(t) \/ Unmark(t)
    \/ \E b \in Branches : GoDark(b)
    \/ Quiet

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(\E t \in Titles : Withdraw(t))
    /\ WF_vars(\E t \in Titles : Unmark(t))

\* A title that has been withdrawn stands exactly once in the deaccession
\* register, however many branches marked it and however often it was marked.
WithdrawnOnce ==
    \A t \in Titles :
        (title[t].state = "withdrawn") =>
            (Cardinality({x \in register : x.ttl = t}) = 1)

EveryMarkEventuallyResolves ==
    \A t \in Titles :
        (title[t].state = "marked") ~>
            (title[t].state = "withdrawn" \/ title[t].state = "held")

====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Titles = {ttlAtlas, ttlPrimer}
    Branches = {brMain, brScience}
    MaxRev = 2
    Copies = 2
    NoBranch = nilBranch

INVARIANT WithdrawnOnce
PROPERTY EveryMarkEventuallyResolves
nl:
A library consortium deaccessions titles from its shared catalogue. Each branch keeps its own catalogue register carrying a revision number, and a branch marks a title for deaccession against the revision its register currently shows.

Withdrawing a title is the irreversible step. The remaining copies are pulped and the shelf mark is retired, so the title can never be withdrawn a second time and nothing can put it back. The write into the deaccession register is a compare-and-swap against the revision the mark was taken on, and a landing write bumps that revision. That check is what stops a title that was marked twice -- because a mark was dropped and taken again -- being pulped twice.

A mark that has gone stale, because the marking branch's register has moved on since, is dropped and the title simply stays on the shelf to be marked again later.

Branch catalogue nodes are not reliable. One branch's node may drop off the consortium without saying so; it then stops confirming anything, and a mark that was taken by that branch is dropped rather than left hanging. The remaining branches carry on deaccessioning normally.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A title that has been withdrawn stands exactly once in the deaccession register, however many branches marked it and however often it was marked and dropped.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every title marked for deaccession is eventually resolved, either withdrawn or put back on the shelf.

---- MODULE W4Od8m1p0t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Nodes, Ledgers, MaxLap, Writes, NoNode

ASSUME NoNode \notin Nodes

VARIABLES node, pen, baton, laps

vars == <<node, pen, baton, laps>>

Typing ==
    /\ node \in [Nodes -> [state : {"idle", "armed", "writing"},
                           done : 0..Writes]]
    /\ pen \in [Ledgers -> [holder : Nodes \cup {NoNode}]]
    /\ baton \in Nodes
    /\ laps \in 0..MaxLap

Init ==
    /\ node = [n \in Nodes |-> [state |-> "idle", done |-> 0]]
    /\ pen = [g \in Ledgers |-> [holder |-> NoNode]]
    /\ baton = CHOOSE n \in Nodes : TRUE
    /\ laps = 0

\* The right to pick up an enrolment pen travels round the ring as a baton.
\* It is only handed on while its holder is not mid-write, so a node cannot
\* lose the baton in the middle of amending a ledger.
Hand(m) ==
    /\ node[baton].state # "writing"
    /\ m # baton
    /\ laps < MaxLap
    /\ baton' = m
    /\ laps' = laps + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<node, pen>>

\* Only the node holding the baton may arm itself to write.
Arm(n) ==
    /\ baton = n
    /\ node[n].state = "idle"
    /\ node[n].done < Writes
    /\ node' = [node EXCEPT ![n].state = "armed"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pen, baton, laps>>

\* Picking up a ledger's pen needs the baton and a pen nobody is holding.
\* Nodes here are slow but never fail: an armed node may take a long time to
\* reach for the pen, and the baton stays with it while it does.
PickUp(n, g) ==
    /\ baton = n
    /\ node[n].state = "armed"
    /\ pen[g].holder = NoNode
    /\ pen' = [pen EXCEPT ![g].holder = n]
    /\ node' = [node EXCEPT ![n].state = "writing"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, laps>>

Amend(n) ==
    /\ node[n].state = "writing"
    /\ node[n].done < Writes
    /\ node' = [node EXCEPT ![n].done = node[n].done + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pen, baton, laps>>

\* A node that armed itself and then lost its turn stands down again.
Disarm(n) ==
    /\ node[n].state = "armed"
    /\ baton # n
    /\ node' = [node EXCEPT ![n].state = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pen, baton, laps>>

PutDown(n, g) ==
    /\ node[n].state = "writing"
    /\ pen[g].holder = n
    /\ pen' = [pen EXCEPT ![g].holder = NoNode]
    /\ node' = [node EXCEPT ![n].state = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, laps>>

Closed ==
    /\ laps = MaxLap
    /\ \A n \in Nodes : node[n].state = "idle"
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E m \in Nodes : Hand(m)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Arm(n) \/ Amend(n) \/ Disarm(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes, g \in Ledgers : PickUp(n, g) \/ PutDown(n, g)
    \/ Closed

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A node that is amending a ledger is holding exactly one pen, so two nodes
\* are never writing the same enrolment ledger at once however slowly the
\* baton goes round.
PenExclusion ==
    \A n \in Nodes :
        (node[n].state = "writing") =>
            (Cardinality({g \in Ledgers : pen[g].holder = n}) = 1)

====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Nodes = {ndArts, ndScience, ndMedicine}
    Ledgers = {lgUnder, lgPost}
    MaxLap = 3
    Writes = 2
    NoNode = nilNode

INVARIANT PenExclusion
nl:
A university runs course registration from several faculty nodes that all amend the same pair of enrolment ledgers, one for undergraduate places and one for postgraduate. A ledger is a critical resource: two nodes amending the same ledger at once would interleave their entries and leave places counted twice.

The nodes take turns by passing a baton round a ring. Only the node holding the baton may arm itself to write, and the baton is only handed on while its holder is not mid-write, so a node cannot have the baton taken out from under it in the middle of amending a ledger. The baton makes a limited number of laps in a registration window.

A node that armed itself and then lost its turn before reaching a pen simply stands down again. An armed node that still has the baton picks up a ledger's pen, and only a pen that nobody is holding. Nodes here are slow but never fail: an armed node may take a long time to reach for the pen and a long time over its entries, and the baton stays with it throughout, but it always gets there in the end. The node then makes its amendments one at a time and finally puts the pen down, leaving the ledger free.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A node that is amending a ledger is holding exactly one pen, so two nodes are never writing the same enrolment ledger at once, however slowly the baton goes round.

---- MODULE W4Od18m0p4t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Passes, Hubs, Cap, MaxRev, NoHub

ASSUME NoHub \notin Hubs

VARIABLES pass, live, rev, dark

vars == <<pass, live, rev, dark>>

Typing ==
    /\ pass \in [Passes -> [state : {"asked", "reading", "granted", "refused",
                                     "expired"},
                            base : 0..MaxRev, hub : Hubs \cup {NoHub}]]
    /\ live \subseteq Passes
    /\ rev \in 0..MaxRev
    /\ dark \subseteq Hubs

Init ==
    /\ pass = [p \in Passes |-> [state |-> "asked", base |-> 0, hub |-> NoHub]]
    /\ live = {}
    /\ rev = 0
    /\ dark = {}

\* A hub reads how many guest passes are live and the revision stamped on that
\* count, then goes away to check the request against the household's rules.
Read(p, h) ==
    /\ pass[p].state = "asked"
    /\ h \notin dark
    /\ pass' = [pass EXCEPT ![p] = [state |-> "reading", base |-> rev, hub |-> h]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<live, rev, dark>>

\* Granting a pass only lands while the revision the hub read is still the one
\* on the count, and only while there is room under the household's limit.
Grant(p) ==
    /\ pass[p].state = "reading"
    /\ pass[p].hub \notin dark
    /\ pass[p].base = rev
    /\ Cardinality(live) < Cap
    /\ rev < MaxRev
    /\ live' = live \cup {p}
    /\ rev' = rev + 1
    /\ pass' = [pass EXCEPT ![p].state = "granted"]
    /\ UNCHANGED dark

\* A request whose read has gone stale, whose hub has dropped off, or that
\* arrives with the household already at its limit, is refused outright.
Refuse(p) ==
    /\ pass[p].state = "reading"
    /\ \/ pass[p].base # rev
       \/ pass[p].hub \in dark
       \/ Cardinality(live) = Cap
       \/ rev = MaxRev
    /\ pass' = [pass EXCEPT ![p].state = "refused"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<live, rev, dark>>

\* A live pass is handed back when the guest leaves, freeing a slot.
Expire(p) ==
    /\ p \in live
    /\ rev < MaxRev
    /\ live' = live \ {p}
    /\ rev' = rev + 1
    /\ pass' = [pass EXCEPT ![p].state = "expired"]
    /\ UNCHANGED dark

\* One hub may drop off the home mesh without saying so.
GoDark(h) ==
    /\ dark = {}
    /\ Cardinality(Hubs) > 1
    /\ dark' = {h}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pass, live, rev>>

Quiet ==
    /\ \A p \in Passes : pass[p].state \in {"granted", "refused", "expired"}
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Passes, h \in Hubs : Read(p, h)
    \/ \E p \in Passes : Grant(p) \/ Refuse(p) \/ Expire(p)
    \/ \E h \in Hubs : GoDark(h)
    \/ Quiet

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(\E p \in Passes, h \in Hubs : Read(p, h))
    /\ WF_vars(\E p \in Passes : Grant(p))
    /\ WF_vars(\E p \in Passes : Refuse(p))

\* Whenever a guest pass is live, the household is holding no more live passes
\* than its limit allows, however many hubs raced each other to grant one.
PassCapacityRespected ==
    \A p \in Passes :
        (pass[p].state = "granted") => (Cardinality(live) <= Cap)

EveryRequestEventuallyAnswered ==
    \A p \in Passes :
        (pass[p].state = "asked") ~>
            (pass[p].state = "granted" \/ pass[p].state = "refused")

====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Passes = {psPlumber, psSitter, psCleaner}
    Hubs = {hubHall, hubGarage}
    Cap = 1
    MaxRev = 3
    NoHub = nilHub

INVARIANT PassCapacityRespected
PROPERTY EveryRequestEventuallyAnswered
nl:
A smart-home door lock network issues temporary guest passes -- for a plumber, a sitter, a cleaner -- and the household has set a hard limit on how many passes may be live at once. Going past that limit is exactly the failure the household bought the system to avoid, so the number of live passes must never exceed it however many hubs are working at the same time.

The count of live passes is kept optimistically rather than under a lock, because it is read far more often than written. A hub reads how many passes are live together with the revision stamped on that count, and then goes away to check the request against the household's rules, which takes a while.

Granting a pass lands only while the revision the hub read is still the one on the count and there is still room under the limit; landing bumps the revision. A request whose read has gone stale, whose hub has dropped off the mesh, that arrives with the household already at its limit, or that arrives after the count has been stamped for the last time in the window, is refused outright rather than retried indefinitely.

A live pass is handed back when the guest leaves, which frees a slot and bumps the count's revision as well. Hubs on a home mesh are not reliable: one hub may drop off without saying so, after which it grants nothing further and any request it was checking is refused; the remaining hubs carry on.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a guest pass is live, the household is holding no more live passes than its limit allows, however many hubs raced each other to grant one.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every guest pass request is eventually answered, either granted or refused.

---- MODULE W4Od9m9p1t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Setpoints, Stations, MaxEpoch, ForceCap

VARIABLES entry, journal, epoch, forced

vars == <<entry, journal, epoch, forced>>

Typing ==
    /\ entry \in [Setpoints -> [state : {"draft", "applied", "dropped"},
                                ep : 0..MaxEpoch]]
    /\ journal \in [Stations -> SUBSET Setpoints]
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ forced \in 0..ForceCap

Init ==
    /\ entry = [p \in Setpoints |-> [state |-> "draft", ep |-> 0]]
    /\ journal = [s \in Stations |-> {}]
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ forced = 0

\* A setpoint is applied at a substation only under the scheme epoch it was
\* drafted against; applying writes it into that station's journal, which is
\* what the protection relays read back.
Apply(p, s) ==
    /\ entry[p].state = "draft"
    /\ entry[p].ep = epoch
    /\ journal' = [journal EXCEPT ![s] = journal[s] \cup {p}]
    /\ entry' = [entry EXCEPT ![p].state = "applied"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, forced>>

\* The privileged override: the control engineer may push a setpoint drafted
\* under an older scheme through anyway when the grid is close to shedding.
\* It still goes into exactly one station journal, and there are only so many
\* overrides in a shift.
Force(p, s) ==
    /\ entry[p].state = "draft"
    /\ entry[p].ep # epoch
    /\ forced < ForceCap
    /\ journal' = [journal EXCEPT ![s] = journal[s] \cup {p}]
    /\ entry' = [entry EXCEPT ![p].state = "applied"]
    /\ forced' = forced + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED epoch

\* A setpoint drafted under a scheme that has since been superseded, and that
\* nobody has forced through, is dropped rather than applied.
Drop(p) ==
    /\ entry[p].state = "draft"
    /\ entry[p].ep # epoch
    /\ entry' = [entry EXCEPT ![p].state = "dropped"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<journal, epoch, forced>>

Redraft(p) ==
    /\ entry[p].state = "dropped"
    /\ entry' = [entry EXCEPT ![p] = [state |-> "draft", ep |-> epoch]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<journal, epoch, forced>>

\* Re-running the shedding scheme under a strictly newer epoch.  Journals are
\* carried across untouched -- a new scheme changes what will be applied next,
\* never what the relays are already holding.
Rescheme ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<entry, journal, forced>>

\* Station journals are tidied of setpoints that never got applied.
Tidy(s) ==
    /\ journal' = [journal EXCEPT ![s] =
                     {p \in journal[s] : entry[p].state = "applied"}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<entry, epoch, forced>>

Steady ==
    /\ \A p \in Setpoints : entry[p].state = "applied"
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Setpoints, s \in Stations : Apply(p, s) \/ Force(p, s)
    \/ \E p \in Setpoints : Drop(p) \/ Redraft(p)
    \/ \E s \in Stations : Tidy(s)
    \/ Rescheme

\* or a tidy-up.

    Stations = {stMill, stHarbour}
    MaxEpoch = 2

nl:
A regional grid's load shedder pushes protection setpoints -- an under-frequency threshold, an overload trip level -- out to its substations. A setpoint that has been applied is written into that station's journal, and the protection relays read their behaviour back from that journal, so a setpoint that quietly vanished from a journal would be an update lost where it matters most.

The shedding scheme is re-run through the watch, and each re-run carries a strictly newer epoch number. A setpoint is drafted against the scheme epoch standing at the time, and is applied at a substation only under that same epoch. A setpoint drafted under a scheme that has since been superseded, and that nobody has pushed through, is dropped rather than applied, and can be redrafted against the current scheme later.

There is a privileged override: the control engineer may push a setpoint drafted under an older scheme through anyway when the grid is close to shedding and there is no time to redraft. The override still writes the setpoint into exactly one station journal, and there are only so many overrides in a shift.

Re-running the scheme carries the station journals across untouched: a new scheme changes what will be applied next, never what the relays are already holding. Station journals are separately tidied of setpoints that were drafted at them but never applied.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every applied setpoint stands in exactly one station journal, so no setpoint the relays are already holding is carried away by a re-scheme, an override, or a tidy-up.

ASSUME NoShip \notin Ships /\ NoCorridor \notin Corridors

Epochs == 1..MaxEpoch

VARIABLES ship, corridor, lead, seizures

vars == <<ship, corridor, lead, seizures>>

Typing ==
    /\ ship \in [Ships -> [state : {"orbit", "cleared", "transit", "clear"},
                           want : Corridors \cup {NoCorridor}]]
    /\ corridor \in [Corridors -> [holder : Ships \cup {NoShip}]]
    /\ lead \in [ep : 0..MaxEpoch, ship : Ships \cup {NoShip}]
    /\ seizures \in 0..OverrideCap

Init ==
    /\ ship = [s \in Ships |-> [state |-> "orbit", want |-> NoCorridor]]
    /\ corridor = [c \in Corridors |-> [holder |-> NoShip]]
    /\ lead = [ep |-> 0, ship |-> NoShip]
    /\ seizures = 0

\* The swarm elects a lead airframe under a strictly newer epoch each time; the
\* lead is the only aircraft that hands out corridor clearances.
Elect(s, e) ==
    /\ e > lead.ep
    /\ lead' = [ep |-> e, ship |-> s]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ship, corridor, seizures>>

\* Only the lead clears an orbiting airframe into a corridor, and only a
\* corridor that nobody is flying.
Clear(s, c) ==
    /\ lead.ship # NoShip
    /\ ship[s].state = "orbit"
    /\ corridor[c].holder = NoShip
    /\ ship' = [ship EXCEPT ![s] = [state |-> "cleared", want |-> c]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<corridor, lead, seizures>>

Enter(s) ==
    /\ ship[s].state = "cleared"
    /\ corridor[ship[s].want].holder = NoShip
    /\ corridor' = [corridor EXCEPT ![ship[s].want].holder = s]
    /\ ship' = [ship EXCEPT ![s].state = "transit"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lead, seizures>>

Exit(s) ==
    /\ ship[s].state = "transit"
    /\ corridor' = [corridor EXCEPT ![ship[s].want].holder = NoShip]
    /\ ship' = [ship EXCEPT ![s] = [state |-> "clear", want |-> NoCorridor]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lead, seizures>>

\* The privileged override: incident command can seize a corridor for a manned
\* helicopter, which turns any cleared airframe waiting on it back to orbit.
\* It never takes a corridor out from under an airframe already in transit, and
\* there are only so many seizures in a sortie.
Seize(c) ==
    /\ corridor[c].holder = NoShip
    /\ seizures < OverrideCap
    /\ ship' = [s \in Ships |->
                  IF ship[s].state = "cleared" /\ ship[s].want = c
                  THEN [state |-> "orbit", want |-> NoCorridor]
                  ELSE ship[s]]
    /\ seizures' = seizures + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<corridor, lead>>

Quiet ==
    /\ \A s \in Ships : ship[s].state = "clear"
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Ships, e \in Epochs : Elect(s, e)
    \/ \E s \in Ships, c \in Corridors : Clear(s, c)
    \/ \E s \in Ships : Enter(s) \/ Exit(s)
    \/ \E c \in Corridors : Seize(c)
    \/ Quiet

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(\E s \in Ships, e \in Epochs : Elect(s, e))
    /\ WF_vars(\E s \in Ships, c \in Corridors : Clear(s, c))
    /\ WF_vars(\E s \in Ships : Enter(s))
    /\ WF_vars(\E s \in Ships : Exit(s))

\* An airframe in transit is flying exactly one corridor, so two airframes are
\* never in the same corridor at once, across a change of lead or a seizure.
CorridorExclusion ==
    \A s \in Ships :
        (ship[s].state = "transit") =>
            (Cardinality({c \in Corridors : corridor[c].holder = s}) = 1)

EveryOrbitEventuallyClears ==
    \A s \in Ships : (ship[s].state = "orbit") ~> (ship[s].state = "clear")

CONSTANTS

    OverrideCap = 1
    NoShip = nilShip
    NoCorridor = nilCorridor

nl:
A wildfire surveillance swarm runs its airframes through a small set of transit corridors over the burn. A corridor is a critical resource: only one airframe may be flying a corridor at a time, because the corridors are narrow lanes between the drop runs and two aircraft in one lane is a collision.

The swarm elects a lead airframe, and the lead is the only aircraft that hands out corridor clearances. Election is by epoch: an airframe becomes lead by taking an epoch strictly newer than any epoch yet taken, so a lead that is lost or superseded is replaced without any hand-back.

The lead clears an orbiting airframe into a corridor that nobody is flying. A cleared airframe then enters the corridor, provided it is still free when it gets there, flies its run and exits, leaving the corridor free for the next.

There is a privileged override: incident command can seize a corridor for a manned helicopter. Seizing turns any airframe that was cleared for that corridor but has not yet entered it back to orbit, so it will need clearing again. Command never seizes a corridor out from under an airframe already in transit, and there are only so many seizures in a sortie.

SAFETY PROPERTY: An airframe in transit is flying exactly one corridor, so two airframes are never in the same corridor at once, across a change of lead or a seizure by incident command.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every orbiting airframe eventually gets through a corridor and out the other side.

---- MODULE W4Od17m0p6t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Reroutes, Consoles, MaxRev, NoConsole

ASSUME NoConsole \notin Consoles

VARIABLES order, plan, console, applied

vars == <<order, plan, console, applied>>

Typing ==
    /\ order \in [Reroutes -> [state : {"drafted", "checking", "live", "void"},
                               base : 0..MaxRev, by : Consoles \cup {NoConsole}]]
    /\ plan \in [rev : 0..MaxRev, by : Consoles \cup {NoConsole}]
    /\ console \in [Consoles -> 0..MaxRev]
    /\ applied \subseteq [rte : Reroutes, rev : 1..MaxRev]

Init ==
    /\ order = [r \in Reroutes |-> [state |-> "drafted", base |-> 0,
                                    by |-> NoConsole]]
    /\ plan = [rev |-> 0, by |-> NoConsole]
    /\ console = [c \in Consoles |-> 0]
    /\ applied = {}

\* A console reads the routing plan's revision and works a reroute up against
\* it.  Operators here are slow but never fail: that can take a long time, and
\* the plan may move on underneath them while it does.
Draft(r, c) ==
    /\ order[r].state = "drafted"
    /\ console' = [console EXCEPT ![c] = plan.rev]
    /\ order' = [order EXCEPT ![r] = [state |-> "checking", base |-> plan.rev,
                                      by |-> c]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<plan, applied>>

\* A reroute goes live only if the console that worked it up is still reading
\* the revision it drafted against, and that revision is still the plan's.  A
\* console that has fallen behind is a stale participant and its reroute is
\* refused rather than pushed onto the belts.
GoLive(r) ==
    /\ order[r].state = "checking"
    /\ order[r].base = plan.rev
    /\ console[order[r].by] = plan.rev
    /\ plan.rev < MaxRev
    /\ applied' = applied \cup {[rte |-> r, rev |-> plan.rev + 1]}
    /\ plan' = [rev |-> plan.rev + 1, by |-> order[r].by]
    /\ order' = [order EXCEPT ![r].state = "live"]
    /\ UNCHANGED console

Void(r) ==
    /\ order[r].state = "checking"
    /\ \/ order[r].base # plan.rev
       \/ console[order[r].by] # plan.rev
       \/ plan.rev = MaxRev
    /\ order' = [order EXCEPT ![r].state = "void"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<plan, console, applied>>

Redraft(r) ==
    /\ order[r].state = "void"
    /\ order' = [order EXCEPT ![r] = [state |-> "drafted", base |-> 0,
                                      by |-> NoConsole]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<plan, console, applied>>

\* A console catches up with the plan on its own schedule.
Refresh(c) ==
    /\ console[c] # plan.rev
    /\ console' = [console EXCEPT ![c] = plan.rev]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<order, plan, applied>>

\* The pier settles once every reroute is live, or once the plan has been
\* stamped for the last time in the bank.
Quiet ==
    /\ \/ plan.rev = MaxRev
       \/ \A r \in Reroutes : order[r].state = "live"
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Reroutes, c \in Consoles : Draft(r, c)
    \/ \E r \in Reroutes : GoLive(r) \/ Void(r) \/ Redraft(r)
    \/ \E c \in Consoles : Refresh(c)
    \/ Quiet

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every live reroute was pushed onto the belts exactly once, by a console that
\* was up to date with the routing plan at the moment it went live: nothing on
\* the belts came from an operator the plan had already left behind.
NoStaleReroute ==
    \A r \in Reroutes :
        (order[r].state = "live") =>
            (Cardinality({x \in applied : x.rte = r}) = 1)

====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Reroutes = {rrGateSwap, rrChuteSwap}
    Consoles = {csNorth, csSouth}
    MaxRev = 3
    NoConsole = nilConsole

INVARIANT NoStaleReroute
nl:
An airport baggage router works its belts off a routing plan that carries a revision number. Operators at the sorting consoles work reroutes up against the plan -- a gate swap when an aircraft changes stand, a chute swap when a chute jams -- and push them onto the belts.

The plan is not held under a lock. A console reads the plan's revision and works its reroute up against that revision. Operators here are slow but never fail: working a reroute up can take a long time, and the plan may move on underneath the console while it does.

A reroute goes live only if two things still hold: the revision it was drafted against is still the plan's standing revision, and the console that worked it up is itself still reading that revision. A console that has fallen behind the plan is a stale participant, and a reroute from a stale console is refused rather than pushed onto the belts -- pushing it would route bags on a picture of the pier that the router has already left behind. A refused reroute is voided and can be redrafted later.

Consoles catch up with the plan on their own schedule, each at its own pace. A reroute that goes live bumps the plan's revision and records which console pushed it. The pier settles once every reroute is live, or once the plan has been stamped for the last time in the bank.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every live reroute was pushed onto the belts exactly once, by a console that was up to date with the routing plan at the moment it went live, so nothing on the belts came from an operator the plan had already left behind.

---- MODULE W4Od6m5p3t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Jobs, Windows, Panels, Banks, MaxTry, NoJob

ASSUME NoJob \notin Jobs

VARIABLES job, vote, bank, tries

vars == <<job, vote, bank, tries>>

Typing ==
    /\ job \in [Jobs -> [state : {"raised", "polling", "held", "done"},
                         slot : Windows \cup {NoJob}, bank : Banks \cup {NoJob}]]
    /\ vote \in [Panels -> [Windows -> Jobs \cup {NoJob}]]
    /\ bank \in [Banks -> Panels]
    /\ tries \in [Jobs -> 0..MaxTry]

Backers(j) == {p \in Panels : vote[p][job[j].slot] = j}

Init ==
    /\ job = [j \in Jobs |-> [state |-> "raised", slot |-> NoJob, bank |-> NoJob]]
    /\ vote = [p \in Panels |-> [w \in Windows |-> NoJob]]
    /\ bank = [b \in Banks |-> CHOOSE p \in Panels : TRUE]
    /\ tries = [j \in Jobs |-> 0]

\* Two lift banks are managed as independent instances but share one pool of
\* maintenance panels, so both are polling the same panels for the same
\* out-of-service windows.
Raise(j, w, b) ==
    /\ job[j].state = "raised"
    /\ \A p \in Panels : vote[p][w] = NoJob
    /\ job' = [job EXCEPT ![j] = [state |-> "polling", slot |-> w, bank |-> b]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, bank, tries>>

\* A panel writes at most one job into each window on its own sheet, and never
\* rewrites a line it has already filled.
Mark(p, j) ==
    /\ job[j].state = "polling"
    /\ vote[p][job[j].slot] = NoJob
    /\ vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![p][job[j].slot] = j]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<job, bank, tries>>

\* A window is held only on a strict majority of the panels' sheets.  Since any
\* two majorities share a panel and no panel writes a window twice, two jobs
\* can never both hold one window.
Hold(j) ==
    /\ job[j].state = "polling"
    /\ 2 * Cardinality(Backers(j)) > Cardinality(Panels)
    /\ job' = [job EXCEPT ![j].state = "held"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, bank, tries>>

Work(j) ==
    /\ job[j].state = "held"
    /\ job' = [job EXCEPT ![j].state = "done"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, bank, tries>>

\* Each bank rotates which panel it treats as its point of contact.
Rotate(b, p) ==
    /\ bank[b] # p
    /\ bank' = [bank EXCEPT ![b] = p]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<job, vote, tries>>

\* A job that has lost the race for its window -- another job took a majority
\* for it first -- gives that window up and goes back to be raised against a
\* window nobody has started marking.
Withdraw(j) ==
    /\ job[j].state = "polling"
    /\ \E k \in Jobs : k # j /\ job[k].state \in {"held", "done"}
                              /\ job[k].slot = job[j].slot
    /\ job' = [job EXCEPT ![j] = [state |-> "raised", slot |-> NoJob,
                                  bank |-> NoJob]]
    /\ tries' = [tries EXCEPT ![j] = IF tries[j] < MaxTry THEN tries[j] + 1
                                      ELSE MaxTry]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, bank>>

Settled ==
    /\ \A j \in Jobs : job[j].state = "done"
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E j \in Jobs, w \in Windows, b \in Banks : Raise(j, w, b)
    \/ \E p \in Panels, j \in Jobs : Mark(p, j)
    \/ \E j \in Jobs : Hold(j) \/ Work(j) \/ Withdraw(j)
    \/ \E b \in Banks, p \in Panels : Rotate(b, p)
    \/ Settled

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(\E j \in Jobs, w \in Windows, b \in Banks : Raise(j, w, b))
    /\ WF_vars(\E p \in Panels, j \in Jobs : Mark(p, j))
    /\ WF_vars(\E j \in Jobs : Hold(j))
    /\ WF_vars(\E j \in Jobs : Work(j))
    /\ WF_vars(\E j \in Jobs : Withdraw(j))

\* A job that holds an out-of-service window holds a majority of the panels'
\* sheets for it, so the same window is never allocated to two jobs, whichever
\* bank raised them.
NoDoubleWindow ==
    \A j \in Jobs :
        (job[j].state = "held") =>
            (2 * Cardinality(Backers(j)) > Cardinality(Panels))

EveryJobEventuallyDone ==
    \A j \in Jobs : (job[j].state = "polling") ~> (job[j].state = "done")

====
nl:
A skyscraper's two lift banks are managed as independent instances -- a low-rise controller and a high-rise controller -- but they share one pool of maintenance panels. Maintenance work has to be booked into an out-of-service window, and a window can only carry one job: two jobs booked into the same window would put two crews in the same shaft.

A controller raises a job against a window that no panel has started marking yet, and puts it to the panels. Each panel keeps its own booking sheet and writes at most one job into each window on it; once a panel has filled a line for a window it never rewrites that line, whichever controller asks. No panel can see any other panel's sheet.

A job holds its window only once a strict majority of the panels have written it into that window on their own sheets. Because any two majorities of the panels share at least one panel, and no panel ever writes two jobs into one window, two jobs can never both collect a majority for the same window -- and that holds across the two controllers just as it does within one.

Each bank also rotates which panel it treats as its point of contact through the week; that changes who it talks to first and nothing about the sheets. A job that holds its window is worked and finished. A job that loses the race for its window -- because another job took a majority for it first -- gives that window up and goes back to be raised against a window nobody has started marking; the number of such retries a job has made is tracked.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A job that holds an out-of-service window holds a majority of the panels' sheets for that window, so the same window is never allocated to two jobs, whichever bank raised them.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every job put to the panels is eventually worked and finished.

EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Feeders, Agents, Horizon, LeaseTicks, NoAgent

ASSUME NoAgent \notin Agents

Clip(n) == IF n < Horizon THEN n ELSE Horizon

VARIABLES feeder, lease, trips, clock, dark

vars == <<feeder, lease, trips, clock, dark>>

Typing ==
    /\ feeder \in [Feeders -> [state : {"closed", "tripped"},
                               by : Agents \cup {NoAgent}]]
    /\ lease \in [Feeders -> [holder : Agents \cup {NoAgent}, until : 0..Horizon]]
    /\ trips \subseteq [fdr : Feeders, agt : Agents]
    /\ clock \in 0..Horizon
    /\ dark \subseteq Agents

Init ==
    /\ feeder = [f \in Feeders |-> [state |-> "closed", by |-> NoAgent]]
    /\ lease = [f \in Feeders |-> [holder |-> NoAgent, until |-> 0]]
    /\ trips = {}
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ dark = {}

\* A shedding agent takes a lease on a feeder that nobody holds.  Leases run
\* out on the clock, so an agent that goes quiet cannot hold a feeder out of
\* the scheme for the rest of the event.
Take(a, f) ==
    /\ a \notin dark
    /\ lease[f].holder = NoAgent
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![f] = [holder |-> a, until |-> Clip(clock + LeaseTicks)]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<feeder, trips, clock, dark>>

\* Tripping a feeder breaker is irreversible: the breaker latches open and only
\* a linesman at the substation can reset it, so it can never be tripped twice.
\* Only an agent holding a live lease on that feeder may trip it.
Trip(a, f) ==
    /\ a \notin dark
    /\ feeder[f].state = "closed"
    /\ lease[f].holder = a
    /\ lease[f].until > clock
    /\ feeder' = [feeder EXCEPT ![f] = [state |-> "tripped", by |-> a]]
    /\ trips' = trips \cup {[fdr |-> f, agt |-> a]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, clock, dark>>

Release(f) ==
    /\ lease[f].holder # NoAgent
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![f] = [holder |-> NoAgent, until |-> 0]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<feeder, trips, clock, dark>>

Tick ==
    /\ clock < Horizon
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<feeder, lease, trips, dark>>

\* A lease the clock has run past is reclaimed so another agent can take the
\* feeder on, whether or not its holder is still answering.
Reclaim(f) ==
    /\ lease[f].holder # NoAgent
    /\ lease[f].until <= clock
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![f] = [holder |-> NoAgent, until |-> 0]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<feeder, trips, clock, dark>>

\* A single agent may lose its link and go quiet without saying so.
GoDark(a) ==
    /\ dark = {}
    /\ Cardinality(Agents) > 1
    /\ dark' = {a}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<feeder, lease, trips, clock>>

Settled ==
    /\ clock = Horizon
    /\ \A f \in Feeders : lease[f].holder = NoAgent
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E a \in Agents, f \in Feeders : Take(a, f) \/ Trip(a, f)
    \/ \E f \in Feeders : Release(f) \/ Reclaim(f)
    \/ \E a \in Agents : GoDark(a)
    \/ Tick
    \/ Settled

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A feeder that has been tripped was tripped exactly once, however many agents
\* held a lease on it before or after, and however many went quiet.
TrippedOnce ==
    \A f \in Feeders :
        (feeder[f].state = "tripped") =>
            (Cardinality({x \in trips : x.fdr = f}) = 1)

    Agents = {agNorth, agSouth}

nl:
A regional grid's load shedder trips feeder breakers when the system runs short. Tripping a breaker is irreversible: the breaker latches open and only a linesman at the substation can reset it, so a feeder that has been tripped can never be tripped again, and a second trip order against it would simply be an error in the record.

Shedding agents take out leases on individual feeders rather than owning them outright. An agent takes a lease on a feeder nobody is holding, and the lease runs out on the clock rather than being held until the agent gives it up, because an agent that goes quiet would otherwise hold a feeder out of the scheme for the rest of the event.

Only an agent holding a live lease on a feeder -- one the clock has not yet run past -- may trip it, and the trip is written to the event log against that agent as it happens. An agent can release a lease early when it decides not to shed that feeder. A lease the clock has run past is reclaimed so another agent can take the feeder on, whether or not its holder is still answering.

Agents are not reliable. A single agent may lose its telemetry link and go quiet without saying so, after which it trips nothing further while its leases simply run out; the remaining agents carry on shedding.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A feeder that has been tripped was tripped exactly once, however many agents held a lease on it before or after, and however many of them went quiet.

---- MODULE W4Od12m9p6t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Depots, MaxEpoch, MaxOrders, Units

ASSUME /\ MaxEpoch \in Nat
       /\ MaxOrders \in Nat
       /\ Units \in Nat
       /\ Cardinality(Depots) >= 2

VARIABLES epoch, agent, inflight, ledger, pool, issued

vars == <<epoch, agent, inflight, ledger, pool, issued>>

\* A withdrawal order carries the identity of its issuer and the
\* accreditation epoch it was stamped with.  The channel is a set, so the
\* tracker may pick orders out of it in any order at all.
Order == [id : 0 .. MaxOrders - 1, dep : Depots, ep : 0 .. MaxEpoch]

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0 .. MaxEpoch
    /\ agent \in Depots
    /\ inflight \subseteq Order
    /\ ledger \subseteq Order
    /\ pool \in 0 .. Units
    /\ issued \in 0 .. MaxOrders

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ agent = CHOOSE d \in Depots : TRUE
    /\ inflight = {}
    /\ ledger = {}
    /\ pool = Units
    /\ issued = 0

\* Reconfiguration advances the epoch and moves accreditation elsewhere.
\* Orders already in flight are deliberately left alone, so they go stale.
Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ \E d \in Depots \ {agent} :
        /\ agent' = d
        /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inflight, ledger, pool, issued>>

Submit ==
    /\ issued < MaxOrders
    /\ inflight' = inflight \cup {[id |-> issued, dep |-> agent, ep |-> epoch]}
    /\ issued' = issued + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, agent, ledger, pool>>

Apply ==
    /\ \E o \in inflight :
        /\ o.ep = epoch
        /\ o.dep = agent
        /\ pool > 0
        /\ ledger' = ledger \cup {o}
        /\ inflight' = inflight \ {o}
        /\ pool' = pool - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, agent, issued>>

Expire ==
    /\ \E o \in inflight :
        /\ o.ep # epoch
        /\ inflight' = inflight \ {o}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, agent, ledger, pool, issued>>

Cancel ==
    /\ \E o \in inflight :
        /\ o.ep = epoch
        /\ inflight' = inflight \ {o}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, agent, ledger, pool, issued>>

\* Once the epoch schedule is exhausted, every order has been issued and
\* the channel is empty, the tracker simply idles.
Idle ==
    /\ epoch = MaxEpoch
    /\ issued = MaxOrders
    /\ inflight = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next == Reconfigure \/ Submit \/ Apply \/ Expire \/ Cancel \/ Idle

Spec == /\ Init
        /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ WF_vars(Apply) /\ WF_vars(Expire) /\ WF_vars(Cancel)

\* A ledger entry stamped with the live epoch has to name the depot that

A central registry designates exactly one depot as the accredited withdrawal agent for the current accreditation epoch; whenever the registry reconfigures, it advances the epoch and names a different depot as the accredited agent. The accredited depot submits withdrawal orders stamped with its own identity and with the epoch under which it was accredited, up to a fixed number of orders overall. Orders travel on an unordered channel, so an order may sit in flight across one or more reconfigurations and arrive long after its issuer has lost accreditation. The tracker applies an in-flight order to the ledger only when the order's stamped epoch is the registry's current epoch, the order's issuer is the currently accredited depot, and unreserved units remain in the pool; applying an order records it on the ledger and decrements the pool. An in-flight order whose stamped epoch no longer matches the registry's epoch is expired and dropped without ever touching the ledger. The accredited depot may also cancel one of its own still-current orders before it is applied. Once the epoch schedule is exhausted, every order has been issued, and the channel is empty, the tracker simply idles. ---- MODULE W4Od3m7p0t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Banks, Batch, NoOwner

ASSUME /\ Batch \in Nat
       /\ NoOwner \notin Banks
       /\ Cardinality(Banks) >= 2

VARIABLES reg, mode, override, remaining

vars == <<reg, mode, override, remaining>>

\* reg is the compare-and-swap ownership register for the settlement window.
\* mode tracks where each member bank is in the acquire/settle cycle.
TypeOK ==
    /\ reg \in Banks \cup {NoOwner}
    /\ mode \in [Banks -> {"idle", "contending", "occupying"}]
    /\ override \in BOOLEAN
    /\ remaining \in [Banks -> 0 .. Batch]

Init ==
    /\ reg = NoOwner
    /\ mode = [b \in Banks |-> "idle"]
    /\ override = FALSE
    /\ remaining = [b \in Banks |-> Batch]

Post(b) ==
    /\ mode[b] = "idle"
    /\ remaining[b] > 0
    /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![b] = "contending"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, override, remaining>>

\* The swap succeeds only against a free register with no override engaged.
Acquire(b) ==
    /\ mode[b] = "contending"
    /\ reg = NoOwner
    /\ ~override
    /\ reg' = b
    /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![b] = "occupying"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<override, remaining>>

Retreat(b) ==
    /\ mode[b] = "contending"
    /\ (reg # NoOwner \/ override)
    /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![b] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, override, remaining>>

Settle(b) ==
    /\ mode[b] = "occupying"
    /\ reg' = NoOwner
    /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![b] = "idle"]
    /\ remaining' = [remaining EXCEPT ![b] = remaining[b] - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED override

\* The supervisor's privileged override frees the register and evicts the
\* current occupant, so the window is empty for the duration of the hold.
Seize ==
    /\ ~override
    /\ override' = TRUE
    /\ reg' = NoOwner
    /\ mode' = [b \in Banks |->
                    IF mode[b] = "occupying" THEN "idle" ELSE mode[b]]
    /\ UNCHANGED remaining

Release ==
    /\ override
    /\ override' = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, mode, remaining>>

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Banks : Post(b) \/ Acquire(b) \/ Retreat(b) \/ Settle(b)
    \/ Seize
    \/ Release

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Occupancy of the settlement window has to be backed by the register.
ExclusiveSettlement ==
    \A b \in Banks : mode[b] = "occupying" => (reg = b /\ ~override)

nl: A clearing house runs an interbank settlement batch. Several member banks each have a number of batch files still to settle, and the settlement window is a single critical resource that only one participant may occupy at a time. Access is arbitrated by a compare-and-swap ownership register that is either free or names exactly one bank. A bank with work left posts an intent to settle, which moves it into the contending state. A contending bank performs the compare-and-swap: if the register is free and the clearing supervisor is not holding an override, the swap succeeds, the register comes to name that bank, and the bank occupies the window. A contending bank whose compare-and-swap would fail -- because the register already names someone or because the supervisor is holding an override -- retreats and will retry later. A bank occupying the window settles one batch file, which decrements its outstanding work, frees the register, and returns the bank to idle. The clearing supervisor has a privileged override: it may seize control at any moment, which frees the register, evicts whichever bank was occupying the window back to idle, and blocks new acquisitions until the supervisor releases the override again. SAFETY PROPERTY: A bank can only be occupying the settlement window if the ownership register names that very bank and the supervisor's override is not engaged.
