EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Machines, StartFloat, StartPurse, NoProposal, NoEscrow

ASSUME /\ StartFloat \in Nat
       /\ StartPurse \in Nat
       /\ Cardinality(Machines) >= 3

VARIABLES float, purse, proposal, votes, escrow

vars == <<float, purse, proposal, votes, escrow>>

Transfers == [from : Machines, to : Machines]

TotalCoins == StartFloat * Cardinality(Machines) + StartPurse

TypeOK ==
    /\ float \in [Machines -> 0 .. TotalCoins]
    /\ purse \in 0 .. StartPurse
    /\ proposal \in {NoProposal} \cup Transfers
    /\ votes \subseteq Machines
    /\ escrow \in {NoEscrow} \cup Machines

\* Every coin in the network sits in exactly one machine float, in the
\* customer purse, or in the single armoured escrow slot.
RECURSIVE FloatSum(_)
FloatSum(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET m == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE
         IN float[m] + FloatSum(S \ {m})

InEscrow == IF escrow = NoEscrow THEN 0 ELSE 1

Init ==
    /\ float = [m \in Machines |-> StartFloat]
    /\ purse = StartPurse
    /\ proposal = NoProposal
    /\ votes = {}
    /\ escrow = NoEscrow

Propose ==
    /\ proposal = NoProposal
    /\ escrow = NoEscrow
    /\ \E t \in Transfers :
        /\ t.from # t.to
        /\ float[t.from] > 0
        /\ proposal' = t
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<float, purse, escrow>>

\* A slow machine is still a live machine: its vote is late, never absent.
Vote ==
    /\ proposal # NoProposal
    /\ \E m \in Machines \ votes : votes' = votes \cup {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<float, purse, proposal, escrow>>

Commit ==
    /\ proposal # NoProposal
    /\ Cardinality(votes) * 2 > Cardinality(Machines)
    /\ float' = [float EXCEPT ![proposal.from] = float[proposal.from] - 1]
    /\ escrow' = proposal.to
    /\ proposal' = NoProposal
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED purse

Deliver ==
    /\ escrow # NoEscrow
    /\ float' = [float EXCEPT ![escrow] = float[escrow] + 1]
    /\ escrow' = NoEscrow
    /\ UNCHANGED <<purse, proposal, votes>>

Purchase ==
    /\ purse > 0
    /\ \E m \in Machines : float' = [float EXCEPT ![m] = float[m] + 1]
    /\ purse' = purse - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<proposal, votes, escrow>>

Next == Propose \/ Vote \/ Commit \/ Deliver \/ Purchase

        /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ WF_vars(Vote) /\ WF_vars(Commit)

\* No rebalancing step may mint or lose a coin along the way.
CoinsConserved == FloatSum(Machines) + purse + InEscrow = TotalCoins

EveryProposalDecided == (proposal # NoProposal) ~> (proposal = NoProposal)

nl: A vending machine network shares one pool of coins. Coins live in exactly three kinds of place: the change float inside each machine, the customer purse that has not yet been spent, and the armoured escrow that holds a transfer while it is on the road between two machines. The operator rebalances floats by proposing a transfer of one coin from a source machine that has a coin to spare to a different destination machine; a proposal can only be raised when no earlier transfer is still in escrow. Every machine in the network then votes on the standing proposal, each machine at most once. Machines in this network are slow but never failed, so a vote that has not arrived yet is merely late. Once a strict majority of the machines have voted, the transfer commits: the coin leaves the source machine's float and enters escrow, and the proposal and its votes are cleared. The escrowed coin is later delivered into the destination machine's float. Independently of all this, a customer may buy an item from any machine, which moves one coin out of the customer purse and into that machine's change float. SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of coins held across all machine floats, the customer purse, and the escrow always equals the number of coins the network started with. LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every transfer proposal that is raised is eventually decided and cleared, because the slow machines always do eventually cast their votes.

EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS NumDesks, Pool, MaxParty

ASSUME /\ NumDesks \in Nat /\ NumDesks >= 2
       /\ Pool \in Nat
       /\ MaxParty \in Nat /\ MaxParty >= 1

Desks == 0 .. NumDesks - 1

\* Desks alternate between the two surgical services around the ring, so
\* both independent services draw beds from the one shared ward pool.
Services == {0, 1}
ServiceOf(d) == d % 2

VARIABLES token, staged, occupied, turnover

vars == <<token, staged, occupied, turnover>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ token \in Desks
    /\ staged \in [Desks -> 0 .. MaxParty]
    /\ occupied \in [Services -> 0 .. Pool]
    /\ turnover \in 0 .. Pool

InUse == occupied[0] + occupied[1] + turnover

Init ==
    /\ token = 0
    /\ staged = [d \in Desks |-> 0]
    /\ occupied = [s \in Services |-> 0]
    /\ turnover = 0

Stage(d) ==
    /\ staged[d] = 0
    /\ \E k \in 1 .. MaxParty : staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![d] = k]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, occupied, turnover>>

PassToken ==
    /\ token' = (token + 1) % NumDesks
    /\ UNCHANGED <<staged, occupied, turnover>>

\* Only the desk currently holding the ring token may confirm, and only if
\* the case still fits beside every other bed that is spoken for.
Book(d) ==
    /\ token = d
    /\ staged[d] > 0
    /\ InUse + staged[d] <= Pool
    /\ occupied' = [occupied EXCEPT ![ServiceOf(d)] = @ + staged[d]]
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![d] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, turnover>>

Withdraw(d) ==
    /\ token = d
    /\ staged[d] > 0
    /\ InUse + staged[d] > Pool
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![d] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, occupied, turnover>>

\* A discharged bed is not free yet -- it is out of service for cleaning.
Discharge(s) ==
    /\ occupied[s] > 0
    /\ occupied' = [occupied EXCEPT ![s] = @ - 1]
    /\ turnover' = turnover + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, staged>>

Cleaned ==
    /\ turnover > 0
    /\ turnover' = turnover - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, staged, occupied>>

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Desks : Stage(d) \/ Book(d) \/ Withdraw(d)
    \/ \E s \in Services : Discharge(s)
    \/ PassToken
    \/ Cleaned

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The shared ward is never oversubscribed by the two services together.
PoolNeverOversubscribed == InUse <= Pool

    Pool = 3

nl: A hospital operating-room scheduler books recovery beds out of a single shared pool. Two independent surgical services run their own booking desks, but both draw beds from the same physical ward, so the pool is shared and its size is fixed. A booking token circulates around the ring of desks and always advances to the next desk in the ring; a desk may only turn a staged case into a confirmed booking during its turn with the token. Any idle desk may stage a case, recording how many recovery beds that case will need. When the desk holding the token has a staged case, it confirms the booking only if the beds already occupied by both services, plus the beds still out of service for turnover, plus the beds the new case needs, all fit inside the pool; confirming adds those beds to that desk's own service and clears the staged case. A desk holding the token whose staged case does not fit withdraws the case instead and clears it. When a service discharges a patient, the bed leaves that service's occupancy but is not immediately available: it moves into turnover. A bed in turnover is returned to the free pool once the ward has finished cleaning it. SAFETY PROPERTY: The beds occupied by the two surgical services together with the beds still in turnover never exceed the size of the shared ward pool.

---- MODULE W4Od12m3p6t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Nodes, Services, MaxOutages, PoolUnits, NoLeader

ASSUME /\ MaxOutages \in Nat
       /\ PoolUnits \in Nat
       /\ NoLeader \notin Nodes
       /\ Cardinality(Nodes) >= 2

VARIABLES coord, term, up, pool, filed, outages

vars == <<coord, term, up, pool, filed, outages>>

\* Terms cannot run away: a service only re-elects after losing its
\* coordinator, and coordinators are only lost to the bounded outage budget.
MaxTerm == 2 * MaxOutages + 1

Records == [svc : Services, node : Nodes, trm : 0 .. MaxTerm]

TypeOK ==
    /\ coord \in [Services -> Nodes \cup {NoLeader}]
    /\ term \in [Services -> 0 .. MaxTerm]
    /\ up \subseteq Nodes
    /\ pool \in 0 .. PoolUnits
    /\ filed \subseteq Records
    /\ outages \in 0 .. MaxOutages

Init ==
    /\ coord = [s \in Services |-> NoLeader]
    /\ term = [s \in Services |-> 0]
    /\ up = Nodes
    /\ pool = PoolUnits
    /\ filed = {}
    /\ outages = 0

Elect ==
    /\ \E s \in Services, n \in up :
        /\ coord[s] = NoLeader
        /\ coord' = [coord EXCEPT ![s] = n]
        /\ term' = [term EXCEPT ![s] = term[s] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<up, pool, filed, outages>>

\* An outage strips the failed node of every coordinator role it held, and
\* closes the term it was serving so no later draw can claim that term.
GoDown ==
    /\ outages < MaxOutages
    /\ \E n \in up :
        /\ up' = up \ {n}
        /\ coord' = [s \in Services |->
                        IF coord[s] = n THEN NoLeader ELSE coord[s]]
        /\ term' = [s \in Services |->
                        IF coord[s] = n THEN term[s] + 1 ELSE term[s]]
    /\ outages' = outages + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, filed>>

ComeBack ==
    /\ \E n \in Nodes \ up : up' = up \cup {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coord, term, pool, filed, outages>>

\* A draw is filed under the term it was taken in, so a record outlives the
\* coordinator that filed it.
Draw ==
    /\ pool > 0
    /\ \E s \in Services :
        /\ coord[s] \in up
        /\ filed' = filed \cup
                    {[svc |-> s, node |-> coord[s], trm |-> term[s]]}
    /\ pool' = pool - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coord, term, up, outages>>

Idle ==
    /\ pool = 0
    /\ outages = MaxOutages
    /\ up = Nodes
    /\ \A s \in Services : coord[s] # NoLeader
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next == Elect \/ GoDown \/ ComeBack \/ Draw \/ Idle

Spec == /\ Init
        /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ WF_vars(Elect) /\ WF_vars(ComeBack)

\* A current-term draw must still be backed by a live, still-elected node.
NoStaleDraw ==
    \A r \in filed :
        r.trm = term[r.svc] => (coord[r.svc] = r.node /\ r.node \in up)

CoordinatorRestored ==
    \A s \in Services : (coord[s] = NoLeader) ~> (coord[s] # NoLeader)

Each service elects its own coordinator from the same set of tracker nodes, and each service keeps its own term number that advances by one every time it elects. A node that is up may go down, up to a bounded number of outages overall; when a node goes down, any service that had elected it is left without a coordinator and immediately closes the term that node was serving by advancing its term number. A service with no coordinator elects any node that is currently up and advances its term. A node that is down may come back up at any time. Once the outage budget is spent, every node is up, both services have coordinators, and the pool is empty, the tracker simply idles. LIVENESS PROPERTY: A service that is left without a coordinator eventually has one again, because nodes always come back up and a service with no coordinator always eventually elects.

EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Agents, MaxTick, LeaseLen, MaxFence, NoLease

ASSUME /\ MaxTick \in Nat
       /\ LeaseLen \in Nat /\ LeaseLen >= 1
       /\ MaxFence \in Nat /\ MaxFence >= 2
       /\ Cardinality(Agents) >= 2

VARIABLES clock, lease, nextFence, staged, crossFence, tape

vars == <<clock, lease, nextFence, staged, crossFence, tape>>

Leases == [holder : Agents, exp : 0 .. MaxTick, fen : 1 .. MaxFence]
Results == [by : Agents, fen : 1 .. MaxFence]

TypeOK ==
    /\ clock \in 0 .. MaxTick
    /\ lease \in {NoLease} \cup Leases
    /\ nextFence \in 1 .. MaxFence + 1
    /\ staged \subseteq Results
    /\ crossFence \in 0 .. MaxFence
    /\ tape \subseteq Results

Expired == lease # NoLease /\ clock > lease.exp

Init ==
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ lease = NoLease
    /\ nextFence = 1
    /\ staged = {}
    /\ crossFence = 0
    /\ tape = {}

Tick ==
    /\ clock < MaxTick
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, nextFence, staged, crossFence, tape>>

\* Fencing numbers only ever move forward, so a lease that has been
\* superseded can never be confused with the one on the books.
Grant ==
    /\ lease = NoLease \/ Expired
    /\ nextFence <= MaxFence
    /\ \E a \in Agents :
        lease' = [holder |-> a,
                  exp |-> IF clock + LeaseLen > MaxTick
                          THEN MaxTick ELSE clock + LeaseLen,
                  fen |-> nextFence]
    /\ nextFence' = nextFence + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, staged, crossFence, tape>>

\* A slow agent is never a dead agent: its staged result is kept forever and
\* may be offered long after the lease it computed under has lapsed.
Compute ==
    /\ lease # NoLease
    /\ staged' = staged \cup {[by |-> lease.holder, fen |-> lease.fen]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, lease, nextFence, crossFence, tape>>

Print ==
    /\ crossFence = 0
    /\ lease # NoLease
    /\ ~Expired
    /\ \E r \in staged :
        /\ r.fen = lease.fen
        /\ r.by = lease.holder
        /\ crossFence' = r.fen
        /\ tape' = tape \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, lease, nextFence, staged>>

Close ==
    /\ clock = MaxTick
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next == Tick \/ Grant \/ Compute \/ Print \/ Close

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The tape can never disagree with the recorded cross, which is only
\* possible if a single cross was ever printed.
CrossPrintedOnce == \A r \in tape : r.fen = crossFence

When there is no lease, or the lease on the books has run past its expiry tick, the exchange may grant a fresh lease to any calculation agent; the fresh lease records its holder, an expiry tick, and a fencing number taken from a counter that only ever moves forward, so the exchange has a bounded number of leases to hand out. ---- MODULE W4Od11m9p1t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS NumJobs, MaxEpoch, MaxSlips

ASSUME /\ NumJobs \in Nat /\ NumJobs >= 2
       /\ MaxEpoch \in Nat
       /\ MaxSlips \in Nat /\ MaxSlips >= 1

Jobs == 1 .. NumJobs

\* A job's page count is simply its job number.
RECURSIVE PageSum(_)
PageSum(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET j == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN j + PageSum(S \ {j})

TotalPages == PageSum(Jobs)

VARIABLES tally, folded, epoch, slips, override, budget

vars == <<tally, folded, epoch, slips, override, budget>>

Slips == [job : Jobs, base : 0 .. TotalPages, ep : 0 .. MaxEpoch]

TypeOK ==
    /\ tally \in 0 .. TotalPages
    /\ folded \subseteq Jobs
    /\ epoch \in 0 .. MaxEpoch
    /\ slips \subseteq Slips
    /\ override \in BOOLEAN
    /\ budget \in 0 .. MaxSlips

Init ==
    /\ tally = 0
    /\ folded = {}
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ slips = {}
    /\ override = FALSE
    /\ budget = MaxSlips

\* Reconfiguration advances the epoch and leaves outstanding slips behind.
Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ ~override
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tally, folded, slips, override, budget>>

Read ==
    /\ budget > 0
    /\ \E j \in Jobs \ folded :
        /\ \A s \in slips : s.job # j
        /\ slips' = slips \cup {[job |-> j, base |-> tally, ep |-> epoch]}
    /\ budget' = budget - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tally, folded, epoch, override>>

\* The clerk writes back the value it computed from what it read, so the
\* epoch-and-value check is the only thing standing between the shop and a
\* lost update.
Redeem ==
    /\ ~override
    /\ \E s \in slips :
        /\ s.ep = epoch
        /\ s.base = tally
        /\ s.job \notin folded
        /\ tally' = s.base + s.job
        /\ folded' = folded \cup {s.job}
        /\ slips' = slips \ {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, override, budget>>

Tear ==
    /\ \E s \in slips :
        /\ (s.ep # epoch \/ s.base # tally \/ s.job \in folded)
        /\ slips' = slips \ {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tally, folded, epoch, override, budget>>

Engage ==
    /\ ~override
    /\ override' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tally, folded, epoch, slips, budget>>

Release ==
    /\ override
    /\ override' = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tally, folded, epoch, slips, budget>>

\* The manager's privileged fold invalidates every slip on the board.
AdminFold ==
    /\ override
    /\ \E j \in Jobs \ folded :
        /\ tally' = tally + j
        /\ folded' = folded \cup {j}
    /\ slips' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, override, budget>>

Next ==
    \/ Reconfigure \/ Read \/ Redeem \/ Tear
    \/ Engage \/ Release \/ AdminFold

Spec == /\ Init
        /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ SF_vars(Redeem) /\ WF_vars(Tear) /\ WF_vars(Release)

\* The record and the fold set can never drift apart.
NoLostUpdate == tally = PageSum(folded)

SlipBoardDrains == (slips # {}) ~> (slips = {})

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    NumJobs = 3
    MaxEpoch = 1
    MaxSlips = 3

PROPERTY SlipBoardDrains
nl: A print shop spooler keeps one shared record: the running page tally for the day, together with the set of jobs whose pages have already been folded into that tally. Job numbers run from one upward and a job's page count is its own number. The spooler runs under a configuration epoch that the shop may advance a bounded number of times; advancing the epoch is a reconfiguration and it deliberately leaves outstanding work alone. A clerk picks up a job that has not been folded in yet and for which no slip is already outstanding, and writes a slip recording the job, the tally value the clerk read, and the epoch that was current when the clerk read it. The shop only allows a bounded number of slips to be written in a day. A clerk redeems a slip only when the override is not engaged, the slip's epoch is still the current epoch, the tally has not moved since the clerk read it, and the job is still unfolded; redeeming writes back the value the clerk computed from what it read and marks the job folded. A slip whose epoch is stale, whose recorded tally no longer matches the record, or whose job has already been folded is torn up. The shop manager has a privileged override: engaging it blocks clerk redemptions, releasing it unblocks them, and while it is engaged the manager may fold any unfolded job into the tally directly, which also tears up every outstanding slip. SAFETY PROPERTY: The page tally always equals the sum of the page counts of exactly those jobs recorded as folded in, so no clerk's update is ever lost or double counted. LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever slips are outstanding, they are eventually all resolved -- redeemed or torn up -- so the slip board always empties again.

CONSTANTS NumCabins, NumBlocks, MaxOutstanding, NoCabin, NoBlock

ASSUME /\ NumCabins \in Nat /\ NumCabins >= 3
       /\ NumBlocks \in Nat /\ NumBlocks >= 1
       /\ MaxOutstanding \in Nat

Cabins == 0 .. NumCabins - 1
Blocks == 1 .. NumBlocks

\* The two line control instances run over the same ring of cabins and draw
\* their track blocks from the one shared pool.
Lines == {0, 1}
LineOf(c) == c % 2

VARIABLES token, enrolled, holder, request

vars == <<token, enrolled, holder, request>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ token \in [Lines -> Cabins]
    /\ enrolled \subseteq Cabins
    /\ holder \in [Blocks -> Cabins \cup {NoCabin}]
    /\ request \in [Cabins -> Blocks \cup {NoBlock}]

Outstanding == Cardinality({c \in Cabins : request[c] # NoBlock})

Init ==
    /\ token = [l \in Lines |-> l]
    /\ enrolled = Cabins
    /\ holder = [b \in Blocks |-> NoCabin]
    /\ request = [c \in Cabins |-> NoBlock]

Advance(l) ==
    /\ token' = [token EXCEPT ![l] = (token[l] + 1) % NumCabins]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<enrolled, holder, request>>

Ask(c) ==
    /\ c \in enrolled
    /\ request[c] = NoBlock
    /\ \E b \in Blocks :
        /\ holder[b] = NoCabin
        /\ request' = [request EXCEPT ![c] = b]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, enrolled, holder>>

\* A cabin may only convert a request while it holds its own line's token.
Reserve(c) ==
    /\ c \in enrolled
    /\ token[LineOf(c)] = c
    /\ request[c] # NoBlock
    /\ holder[request[c]] = NoCabin
    /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![request[c]] = c]
    /\ request' = [request EXCEPT ![c] = NoBlock]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, enrolled>>

Free(c) ==
    /\ \E b \in Blocks :
        /\ holder[b] = c
        /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![b] = NoCabin]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, enrolled, request>>

\* Striking a cabin off the roll must also strip it of everything it holds.
Withdraw(c) ==
    /\ c \in enrolled
    /\ enrolled' = enrolled \ {c}
    /\ holder' = [b \in Blocks |->
                     IF holder[b] = c THEN NoCabin ELSE holder[b]]
    /\ request' = [request EXCEPT ![c] = NoBlock]
    /\ UNCHANGED token

Reinstate(c) ==
    /\ c \notin enrolled
    /\ enrolled' = enrolled \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, holder, request>>

Next ==
    \/ \E l \in Lines : Advance(l)
    \/ \E c \in Cabins : Ask(c) \/ Reserve(c) \/ Free(c)
                          \/ Withdraw(c) \/ Reinstate(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Cabins may raise requests freely; the bound on how many route requests
\* are examined at once is what keeps the reachable state space small.
RequestBound == Outstanding <= MaxOutstanding

\* A block in the shared pool is only ever held by a cabin still in service.
NoWithdrawnHolder ==
    \A b \in Blocks : holder[b] # NoCabin => holder[b] \in enrolled

nl: A subway signalling system reserves track blocks out of one shared pool. Two independent line control instances run over the same ring of interlocking cabins, and each line circulates its own movement-authority token around that ring; a token always advances to the next cabin in the ring. Cabins are numbered, and a cabin belongs to the line matching the parity of its number. Only cabins that are currently enrolled in service may take part. An enrolled cabin that has no route request outstanding may raise a request for a block that is not currently reserved, and only situations in which at most two route requests are outstanding at once are considered. An enrolled cabin turns its outstanding request into a reservation only while it is holding its own line's token and the requested block is still unreserved; the block then records that cabin as its holder and the request is cleared. A cabin may release a block it holds back to the pool at any time. The signalling office may withdraw an enrolled cabin from service, which strikes it off the roll, drops its outstanding request, and returns every block it was holding to the pool. A cabin that has been withdrawn may later be reinstated onto the roll. SAFETY PROPERTY: Every reserved track block is held by a cabin that is still enrolled in service, so no withdrawn cabin ever retains a movement authority.

---- MODULE W4Od7m3p2t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Cranes, Berths, StartAboard, MaxFailures, NoLead

ASSUME /\ StartAboard \in Nat /\ StartAboard >= 1
       /\ MaxFailures \in Nat
       /\ NoLead \notin Cranes
       /\ Cardinality(Cranes) > Cardinality(Berths)

VARIABLES lead, inService, aboard, ashore, spreader, failures

vars == <<lead, inService, aboard, ashore, spreader, failures>>

TotalBoxes == StartAboard * Cardinality(Berths)

RECURSIVE Tally(_, _)
Tally(f, S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET b == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN f[b] + Tally(f, S \ {b})

TypeOK ==
    /\ lead \in [Berths -> Cranes \cup {NoLead}]
    /\ inService \subseteq Cranes
    /\ aboard \in [Berths -> 0 .. TotalBoxes]
    /\ ashore \in [Berths -> 0 .. TotalBoxes]
    /\ spreader \in [Berths -> 0 .. 1]
    /\ failures \in 0 .. MaxFailures

Init ==
    /\ lead = [b \in Berths |-> NoLead]
    /\ inService = Cranes
    /\ aboard = [b \in Berths |-> StartAboard]
    /\ ashore = [b \in Berths |-> 0]
    /\ spreader = [b \in Berths |-> 0]
    /\ failures = 0

\* The berths are independent but the crane pool is shared, so a crane can
\* lead at most one berth at a time.
ElectAt(b) ==
    /\ lead[b] = NoLead
    /\ \E c \in inService :
        /\ \A o \in Berths : lead[o] # c
        /\ lead' = [lead EXCEPT ![b] = c]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inService, aboard, ashore, spreader, failures>>

\* A crane can only be taken out of service with an empty spreader, so no
\* box is ever stranded by a failover.
Fail ==
    /\ failures < MaxFailures
    /\ \E c \in inService :
        /\ \A b \in Berths : lead[b] = c => spreader[b] = 0
        /\ inService' = inService \ {c}
        /\ lead' = [b \in Berths |->
                       IF lead[b] = c THEN NoLead ELSE lead[b]]
    /\ failures' = failures + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<aboard, ashore, spreader>>

Restore ==
    /\ \E c \in Cranes \ inService : inService' = inService \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lead, aboard, ashore, spreader, failures>>

\* One straddle gang serves both berths, so only one spreader may be loaded
\* at a time even though the berths are otherwise independent.
LiftAt(b) ==
    /\ lead[b] \in inService
    /\ \A o \in Berths : spreader[o] = 0
    /\ aboard[b] > 0
    /\ aboard' = [aboard EXCEPT ![b] = aboard[b] - 1]
    /\ spreader' = [spreader EXCEPT ![b] = 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lead, inService, ashore, failures>>

LandAt(b) ==
    /\ lead[b] \in inService
    /\ spreader[b] = 1
    /\ spreader' = [spreader EXCEPT ![b] = 0]
    /\ ashore' = [ashore EXCEPT ![b] = ashore[b] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lead, inService, aboard, failures>>

ReloadAt(b) ==
    /\ ashore[b] > 0
    /\ ashore' = [ashore EXCEPT ![b] = ashore[b] - 1]
    /\ aboard' = [aboard EXCEPT ![b] = aboard[b] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lead, inService, spreader, failures>>

Land == \E b \in Berths : LandAt(b)

Next ==
    \/ Fail \/ Restore \/ Land
    \/ \E b \in Berths : ElectAt(b) \/ LiftAt(b) \/ ReloadAt(b)

Spec == /\ Init
        /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ WF_vars(Land)

\* Every box is aboard, ashore, or on a spreader -- never anywhere else.
BoxesConserved ==
    Tally(aboard, Berths) + Tally(ashore, Berths)
        + Tally(spreader, Berths) = TotalBoxes

SpreadersAlwaysClear ==
    (\E b \in Berths : spreader[b] = 1) ~> (\A b \in Berths : spreader[b] = 0)

====

nl: A container-ship crane yard works two berths at once. The two berth control instances are independent, but they draw their gantry cranes from one shared pool, and a crane can be the elected lead of at most one berth at a time. Every container in the yard is in exactly one of three places: still aboard the ship at its berth, stacked ashore on that berth's quay, or hanging on that berth's spreader between the two. A berth that has no lead elects any crane that is in service and is not already leading the other berth. A crane may be taken out of service, up to a bounded number of failures for the whole yard, but only when the berth it leads has an empty spreader; taking it out of service leaves that berth without a lead. A crane that is out of service may be brought back into service at any time. One straddle gang serves the whole yard, so a berth whose lead is in service may lift one container off the ship onto its spreader only while every spreader in the yard is empty. A berth whose lead is in service and whose spreader is loaded may land that container onto the quay stack. A container stacked ashore may be reloaded back aboard the ship at the same berth. SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of containers aboard the ships, stacked on the quays, and hanging on the spreaders always adds up to the number of containers the yard started with. LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever a container is hanging on a spreader, the yard eventually reaches a point where every spreader is clear again.
